בין הערבים. מלה קשה, ורבינו שלמה אמר, כי רגע נטות השמש ומחצי היום לצד מערב ולא נתן טעם למה ערבים שנים, והנה כתוב, ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות בין הערבים (למטה ל, ה), ואין ספק כי בשקוע השמש ידליק את הנרות, וכאשר חפשנו זאת המלה מצאנו כי יקרא רגע בין הערבים ערב, כי כן כתוב, בין הערבים תאכלו בשר (טז יב), ושם כתוב, בתת ה' לכם בערב בשר לאכול, (שם שם ח) ובהדלקת הנרות כתוב, יערוך אותו אהרן ובניו מערב עד בקר (כז כא), וכתיב עולות לה', לבקר ולערב (עזרא ג ג), וכתיב "ואת הכבש השני תעשה בין הערבים" (למטה כט לט), והנה על הפסח שכתוב בו בין הערבים, מצאנו "שם תזבח את הפסח בערב, כבא השמש מועד צאתך ממצרים" (דבר' טז ו), פי' כבא השמש לצד מערב ואין זה משמע ביאה, כי הוא היפך יציאת השמש, מדכתיב, השמש יצא על הארץ (ברא' יט כג) שהחל להראות על הארץ, וככה, ובא השמש וטהר (ויקרא כב ז) שלא יראה על הארץ, והנה כתוב על מקרה לילה, והיה לפנות ערב ירחץ במים (דבר' כג יב), ואם אין הדבר כן, יבאר לנו מה הפרש יש בין כבוא השמש של פסח, ובין כבוא השמש של מקרה לילה, וככה ובא השמש וטהר (ויקרא כב ז), אמרו המינים כי שלשה ערבים הם וראייתם בעבור שמצאו, עד הערב השלישית (ש"א ב, ה), והם לא הכירו האמת ולא הבינו, כי כתוב, מחר חדש וגו' ושלשת תרד מאוד (שם שם יה יט) שפירושו כאשר יהיה היום השלישי מהיום הסמוך לערב השדה שאתה נסתר שם, ובעבור זה אמר עד הערב השלישי, ועתה אשוב לפרש, דע כי משקל ערבים לעולם נופל על משקל שנים כמו אָבְנָיִם (למעלה א טז) וכמוהו לוחתָיִם (יחז' כז ה) וככה דְרָכַיִם (משלי כח ו), והעד יפול באחת (שם) וככה שמים, כי הם שני סדני הגלגל שהם כמו מסמרות נטועים שעליהם משענות הגלגל וככה לנטוע שמים (ישעי' נא טז), וכבר פירשתי בס' השם הנכבד, כי שמים מגזרת שם ישר נכח עמו (איוב כג ז), רמז לשני מקומות, והנה יש לנו שני ערבים האחד עריבת השמש, והוא עת ביאתו תחת הארץ, והשני ביאת אורו הנראה בעבים והנה יש ביניהם קרוב משעה ושליש שעה, אז יבא בעל קרי אל המחנה וידליק אהרן את הנרות אמר הגאון רב סעדיה ז"ל, מדת מזבח העולה חמש אמות אורך, וחמש אמות רוחב ובמדת הזאת לא יעמדו כי אם כהנים מעטים שהם זורקים דמי הפסחים קודם שיקרשו והנה בימי יאשיהו שהיו ישראל מועטים לא יכלו הכהנים לזרוק דמי הפסחים והשלמים ששחטו לזרקם לשעה ושליש שעה, ואף כי בהיות כל השבטים בארצם, והנה היתה קבלה שיחלו לשחוט מהרגע שיתברר לאדם כי השמש נטה לצד מערב והזכיר הכתוב בין הערבים שרוב הפסחים היו אז נשחטים שם, והוא סוף הזמן שלא יעבור עד עריבת אור השמש:


AT DUSK. *Ben ha-arbayim* (at dusk) is a difficult phrase. Rabbi Solomon¹⁹⁶. says that it refers to the moment after midday that the sun moves to the west. He does not explain why *arbayim* is in the dual form.¹⁹⁷ refers to those hours between the darkening of the day (*arivat ha-yom*, i.e., when the sun begins its descent) and the darkening of the night (*arivat ha-laylah*, i.e., when night starts). The day darkens at the start of the seventh hour…and the night begins to darken at the beginning of the night.” Hence according to Rashi, *ben ha-arbayim* means between the two evenings (or darkenings). I.E. probably quoted from memory. I doubt that I.E.’s manuscript of Rashi differed from ours. Now, Scripture states, *And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at dusk* (ben ha-arbayim) (Ex. 30:8), and there is no doubt that Aaron is to light the lamps when the sun sets.¹⁹⁸ does not refer to a moment after midday. Now, when we researched this phrase we found that Scripture refers to the moment of *ben ha-arbayim* as *erev* (evening).¹⁹⁹ For it is clearly written, *At dusk* (ben ha-arbayim) *ye shall eat flesh* (Ex. 16:12), and it is there stated, *when the Lord shall give you in the evening* (ba-erev) *flesh to eat* (Ex. 16:8). Likewise, concerning the lighting of the lamps it is written: *Aaron and his sons shall set it in order, to burn from evening* (erev) *to morning before the Lord* (Ex. 27:21).²⁰⁰ means the same as *ben ha-arbayim*, as this verse is parallel to Ex. 30:8. It is similarly written, *even burnt-offerings mornings and evening* (erev) (Ezra 3:3), and it is stated, *The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at dusk* (ben ha-arbayim) (Ex. 29:39). Now concerning the Passover sacrifice, about which the term *ben ha-arbayim* (at dusk) is employed, we find that Scripture states, *there thou shalt sacrifice the passover-offering at even* (erev), *at the coming* (bo)²⁰¹ *of the sun, at the season that thou earnest forth out of Egypt* (Deut. 16:6). Rabbi Solomon²⁰². 38. explains that the reference is to the time that the sun comes to the west.²⁰³ However, this is not the meaning of *bo*. It refers to the opposite of the sun’s going forth upon the earth²⁰⁴ means the setting of the sun. since it is written, *the sun went out* (yatza) *upon the earth* (Gen. 19:23),²⁰⁵ which means the time that the sun first begins to be seen on the earth. Similarly, *And when the sun comes* (ba) *he shall be clean*²⁰⁶ (Lev. 22:7) means when the sun shall no longer be seen upon the ground. Now it is written concerning a nocturnal seminal emission, *But it shall be, when evening cometh on, he shall bathe himself in water; and when the sun comes* (u-khe-vo ha-shemesh)²⁰⁷. *he may come within the camp*²⁰⁸ (Deut. 23:12). If this is not so, then let Rabbi Solomon explain what difference there is between “when the sun comes” with regard to Passover and “when the sun comes” with regard to a nocturnal seminal emission. It is the same with *and when the sun comes he*²⁰⁹ *shall be clean* (Lev. 22:7).²¹⁰ with regard to Passover means a moment after midday and why *when the sun comes* with regard to the laws of ritual purity means after sunset. The Sadducees²¹¹ say that there are three evenings.²¹² Their proof is from a verse which they found to read, *ha-erev ha-shelishit* (the third evening)²¹³ (I Sam. 20:5). However, they do not recognize or understand the truth. It is written, *Tomorrow is the new moon…And in the third day thou shalt hide thyself well* (I Sam. 20:18, 19), the meaning of which is: when close to evening of the third day starting from today comes, you shall hide yourself well in the field where you are presently hidden. It is because of this that Jonathan said, *until the third evening*.²¹⁴ does not mean until the third of the day’s three evenings arrives but rather the evening of the third day arrives. See note 213. I will now backtrack and explain.²¹⁵ means. Know that the word *arbayim* is always vocalized according to the paradigm of the dual forms like *ovnayim* (birthstool) (Ex. 1:16). *Luchotayim* (planks) (Ezek. 27:5) is similar. So is *derachayim* (ways) (Prov. 28:18), as *But he that is perverse in his ways* (derachayim) *shall fall in one of them* (*Ibid.*) proves.²¹⁶ refers to *derachayim*. This shows that *derachayim* is a dual form and refers to two. Prov. 28:18 is translated according to I.E. The same is the case with the word *shamayim* (heaven), as the heavens consist of two poles²¹⁷ (anvil). In medieval astronomic terminology *sadan* refers to a pole. See Klatzkin, *op. cit.*, Vol. III, p. 94. which are like fastened nails upon which the sphere leans. I have already explained in *The Book of God*, the Glorious,²¹⁸, chap. 1 in *Yalkut Ibn Ezra*, edited by I. Levin, Israel, 1985. that the word *shamayim* comes from the same root as the word *sham* (there) in *There the upright might reason with Him* (Job 23:7).²¹⁹ to the Arabic word *sammah* (high). The term *shamayim* alludes to these two places.²²⁰ is a dual form. We thus have two evenings: one when the sun sets, that is, the time when the sun descends beneath the earth; the second when its light disappears from the clouds.²²¹, which literally means evenings. Now there is close to one and a third hours between them. It is at this time²²², between the evenings. that one who experienced a seminal emission²²³ may enter the camp and Aaron kindles the lights.²²⁴ Rabbi Saadiah Gaon, of blessed memory, says that the altar of the burnt offering measured five cubits in length and five cubits in width. Such an area has room only for a small number of *kohanim* (priests), who are the ones that sprinkle the blood from the paschal lambs before it coagulates. Now in the days of Josiah,²²⁵ when the number of Israelites were few,²²⁶ the *kohanim* were not able to sprinkle the blood of the Passover offerings and the peace offerings that they slaughtered; i.e., they were not able to sprinkle them on the altar in one and a third hours.²²⁷ on an altar measuring five cubits by five cubits in an hour and a third. How much more unable to do so were they when all the tribes were in their country.²²⁸ There was thus a tradition that they begin to slaughter²²⁹ from the moment that it became clear to a person that the sun turned to the west.²³⁰ 64a. Scripture speaks of *ben ha-arbayim* (at dusk)²³¹ because most of the paschal lambs were slaughtered then,²³² and that marks its time limit;²³³ for one should not wait until the going down of the sun’s light.²³⁴ which starts the night (see above) is the final cut-off point for the slaughtering of the paschal lamb.

ON THE TWO SIDE-POSTS. Of the door of the house. Moses will go on to explain²³⁵ how they are to take the blood.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:7:2)


ומלת משקוף, מגזרת חלון (ברא' ח ו) וישקף (שם כו ה), וזה המשקוף הוא על פתח הבית, וככה מנהג כל ארץ ישמעאל כי מנהג הערלים לא היה כמנהג המצריים ואפילו במאכליהן, כמו "פתות אותה פתים" (ויקרא ב ו), וככה תכשיטי הנשים לשום נזם באף ובאזן, וכל אשר הזכיר ישעיה על בנות ציון, וככה אין בית להם כי אם בחצר, האחת יקרא פתח הבית, והחיצון שער החצר, ורבים אמרו כי נתינת הדם על המשקוף ועל שתי המזוזות, להראות שישחטו תועבת מצרים בפרהסיא, כי כבר נפל פחדם עליהם, ולא יפחדו שיסקלום, ואילו היה כן, היה זה בשער החצר, והנה לא הושם הדם כי אם בסתר, שסגרו שער החצר, והם שחטו בין הערבים שלא יראה אדם שהוא סמוך ללילה, ואיש לא יצא מפתח ביתו עד בקר, שהלכו לדרכם, וסגרו כל אחד שער חצרו, כי המצריים חשבו שישובו, רק הטעם להיות הדם על המשקוף, להיות כופר בעד כל האוכל בבית ויהיה סימן למשחית שיראנו כדרך, והתוית תו (יחז' ט ד):


[LINTEL.] The word *mashkof* (lintel) means a window.²³⁶ as a lintel, namely, “the upper beam against which the door strikes when one closes it.” Rashi compares *mashkof* to the Aramaic words *shakef* (struck) and *mashkofe* (blow). Compare, *va-yashkef* (looked) (Gen. 26:8).²³⁷ because one looks through it. This window was in the door.²³⁸ This is the custom in all Moslem countries. The practice of the uncircumcised²³⁹ differs from that of the Egyptians²⁴⁰ even regarding food,²⁴¹ an example being, *Thou shalt break it in pieces* (Lev. 2:6).²⁴². Thus *pittim* (pieces of pitta) shows that the bread eaten by the two cultures is different. Or, Lev. 2:6 speaks of bread baked in a pan. Europeans do not make bread in that manner. We thus see that different peoples have different food habits. Similarly with regard to women’s jewelry such as the wearing of nose rings and earrings and all that the prophet Isaiah mentioned concerning the daughters of Zion (Is. 3:18-24).²⁴³ Likewise, all of their houses²⁴⁴ without exception are built in courtyards. One entrance is called the door to the house and the other the gate of the courtyard. Many say that the purpose of placing the blood on the window and on the two side-posts was to demonstrate publicly that they slaughtered the abomination of Egypt,²⁴⁵ 6, “*On the two side-posts and on the lintel*. Rabbi Isaac says…on the outside, so that the Egyptians, seeing it, would be cut to the quick.” The *Shulkhan Arukh* uses a similar reason for Shabbat Ha-Gadol. See *Orech Chayyim* 430:1. since by then the fear of the Israelites had fallen on the Egyptians, and the Israelites were not afraid of being stoned.²⁴⁶ Now if this was the case then the blood should have been placed on the entrance to the courtyard.²⁴⁷ However, the blood was placed in secret, for they closed the gate of the courtyard. Furthermore, they slaughtered the lamb at dusk, which is close to night, so that no one would see them. Moreover, no man left his house until the morning when each one went on his way and each one closed the gate to his courtyard. The Egyptians thought that the Israelites would return.²⁴⁸ The reason the blood was smeared on the window was to make atonement²⁴⁹ for all those eating in the house and to serve as a mark for the destroyer²⁵⁰ to see. It is to be understood in the same way as *and set a mark on the foreheads of the men* (Ezek. 9:4).²⁵¹

ומלת בָּתִּים משונה בדקדוק כי יש דגש אחר קמץ גדול, ואין זה משפט הלשון, רק אם היה הקמץ חטף, כמו רָנּוּ שמים (ישעי' מד כג) אולי היה כן בעבור חסרון יו"ד בית, שלא תתערב זאת הגזרה עם גזרת עשרת הַבַּתִּים חומר (יחז' מה יד) שהוא פתח לשון רבים, מן האיפה והבת (שם שם יא), ומלת "על הבתים" יורנו כי הוא מלעיל הפך המנהג:


[HOUSES.] The word *battim* (houses) is grammatically irregular, as it has a *dagesh*²⁵². following a long *kamatz*.²⁵³. This is contrary to the rule²⁵⁴ is not placed in a letter that follows a consonant vocalized with a *kamatz*. whereby a *dagesh* is only placed after a short *kamatz*,²⁵⁵. as in *ronnu* (sing)²⁵⁶ is vocalized with a *kamatz katan*, and a *dagesh*, is placed in the *resh*. in *Sing, O ye heavens* (Is. 44:23). Perhaps *battim* was vocalized with a *kamatz* ²⁵⁷ (houses) should have been vocalized with a *pattach* beneath the *bet*. Hence there is a *dagesh* in the *tav*. because of the missing *yod* in the word *bayit*.²⁵⁸ is *bayit*. The *yod* drops out in the plural. Now if the yod were retained there would be no chance of confusing our word with *battim* meaning baths because our word would have been pronounced *beyatim*. However, since the *yod* drops out in the plural, if both words were identically vocalized one could confuse them. This form²⁵⁹ (houses), the plural of *bayit*. would thus not be confused with the form *battim* (baths) in *ten baths are a homer* (Ezek. 45:14) wherein *battim*, the plural of *bat* (bath) in *The ephah and the bath* (Ezek. 45:11), is vocalized with a *pattach* in the plural.²⁶⁰, meaning houses, was changed from a *pattach* to a *kamatz*. The word *battim* (houses) in *upon the houses* is indicative,²⁶¹ is irregular (Filwarg). Or that its *kamatz* is not a “real” *kamatz* (Krinsky). Or that it indicates why in this word a *dagesh* follows a *kamatz* (Weiser). for unlike the rule it is penultimately accented.²⁶² is not a “real” *kamatz*. If it were, then *battim* would be ultimately accented (Krinsky). Or it shows that a *dagesh* may follow after an accented *kamatz*. Compare, *nashattah* (faileth) in Is. 41:17 (Weiser). It should be noted that *battim* is found penultimately accented only in our verse. Elsewhere in Scripture it is always ultimately accented.

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:8:1)


**על מרורים יאכלהו.** אמר אחד מחכמי ספרד, ידוע כי הליחה תגבר בארץ מצרים בעבור מימי היאור, ובעבור שלא ירד שם גשם, כי האויר הוא לח תמיד, על כן מנהגם היה לאכול בכל שלחנם מיני מרורים רבים מעשבים וחרדל, ואפילו לא היה למצרי אלא פת לבד, לעולם המרורים יהיו על שלחנו לטבול בו הפת, כי הם רפואה לאוירם, ואנחנו נסמוך על דעת קדמונינו ז"ל, שפירשו לנו כי המרורים זכר לוימררו את חייהם (א יד):


WITH BITTER HERBS THEY SHALL EAT IT. One of the Spanish wise men explained that it is well known that because of the Nile and the lack of rain, the humidity in Egypt is very high and the air is always moist. It was therefore their custom to eat all sorts of bitter herbs and mustards with their meals. An Egyptian always had bitters in which to dip his bread, even if he had but one loaf of bread, because the bitters are a cure for their climate.²⁶³ However, we will rely on the opinion of our ancients of blessed memory, who explained to us that the reason for the bitter herbs is to remind us that *they made their lives bitter* (Ex. 1:14).²⁶⁴ 116b.

footnotes:
²⁶³ Hence God commanded the Israelites to eat bitter herbs with the paschal lamb.
²⁶⁴ Pesachim



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:9:1)


**נא.** יש אומרים כאשר הוא עתה שהבשר חי, ובדרך הזאת לא מצאנו בכל המקרא, ואחרים אמרו כי הוא מגזרת כי הניא אביה אותה (במד' ל ו) והטעם שבור, ואין זה נכון, כי אחר כן אמר ועצם לא תשברו בו (פ' מו), והנכון בעיני שאין לו חבר במקרא, ופירושו הפך מבושל, והוא שנקרא חי, כמו, לא יוקח ממך בשר מבושל כי אם חי (ש"א ב טו), וכבר אמרתי כי רוב לשון ערבי דומה ללשון עברית, והבשר החי יקראו בלשון ערבי ניי, ואותיות אהו"י מתחלפים להם בלשונם כמו בלשוננו:


RAW. Some say that the meaning of *na* (raw) is: as it is now,²⁶⁵ means now. See I.E. on Gen. 12:11, “*Na* means now. *Na* in *behold now* (na), *I am old* (Gen. 27.2), and *Woe now* (na) *unto us* (Lam. 5:16) are similar.” i.e., when the meat is raw. However, we do not find the word *na* used in such a way elsewhere in Scripture.²⁶⁶ Others say²⁶⁷ that it comes from the same root as *heni* (breaks)²⁶⁸. in *But if her father breaks her vow* (Num. 30:6) and means broken.²⁶⁹ However, this is incorrect, as Scripture later states, *neither shall ye break a bone thereof* (v. 46).²⁷⁰ However, in my opinion the word *na*²⁷¹ has no counterpart in Scripture. It means the opposite of cooked and is²⁷² referred to as *chai* (raw). Compare, *For he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw* (chai) (I Sam. 2:15). I have previously noted that most of Arabic is similar to Hebrew.²⁷³ Now in Arabic raw meat is called *nayy*, and the *alef heh, vav*, and *yod* interchange in the tongue of the Arabs as it does in our tongue.²⁷⁴ equals *nun alef*.

**ובשל.** שם התואר ופירושו שהוא מבושל במים, כי גם צלי אש יקרא מבושל, כדכתיב ובשלת ואכלת (דבר' טז ז) ויבשלו את הפסח באש כמשפט (דה"ב לה יג), ויתכן להיות ובשל מבושל כמאכל המלכים, על דרך המשקיות, כי ישימו על האש כלי נחשת רחב, וימלאו חציו מים, וכאשר ירתיחו המים ישימו סיר הבשר עם מים קרים על המים הרותחים, וככה יתבשל הבשר וזה המאכל מועיל יותר מכל המאכל אשר יהיה קרוב אל האש, והנני הכותב מוסיף על דברי זה החכם כאשר שמעתי מפיו, ובשל שם התואר על משקל, כבד, זקן,, וככה זה ובשל כי הבי"ת קמוץ והשי"ן רפה, ואינו שם הפועל, על דרך כי כבד אכבדך (במד' כב יז) הַכֵּה תַכֶּה (דבר' יג טז), כי לעולם לא יבוא שם הפועל בהתחברו רק על לשון עבר או עתיד, כמו דַבר ידבר (למעלה ד יד) הַקְדֵשׁ הקדשתי (שופ' יז ג), רק להתחבר שם הפעל עם פועל ופעול לא יבא, והנה זה בָשֵל כמו כָבֵד, ולנקבה הזרוע בְשֵלָה (במד' ו יט), ואל תתמה מה צורך לומר שני הענינים בשל ומבושל, כי שני בישולים הם כמו שפירש האחד להכניס כלי שהבשר בתוכו בתוך כלי המים הרותחין ולרבים, בשלים מבושלים והמה חכמים, מחוכמים (משלי ל כד), וככה יאמר ליחיד חכם מחוכם, ברוך ומבורך והפרש יש בין בדיקות הלשון בין חכם למחוכם, וככה בין לבָשֵל ומבושל כאשר פירש:


NOR SODDEN. *Bashel* (sodden) is an adjective. Here its meaning is, that which is sodden with water.²⁷⁵ (nor sodden at all with water), which literally means, nor boiled, boiled in water. That which is roasted in fire is also called *mevushal*,²⁷⁶ (boiled in water). for it is written, *And thou shalt roast* (u-vishalta)²⁷⁷ refers to roasting, as it is forbidden to cook the paschal lamb in water. *and eat it* (Deut. 16:7) and, *And they roasted* (va-yevashelu)²⁷⁸ *the passover with fire according to the ordinance* (II Chron. 35:13). It is possible that *nor sodden at all with water*²⁷⁹ (nor boiled in water). Why be redundant and write *u-vashel mevushal ba-mayim*, and boiled, boiled in water. means nor cooked, that is, cooked in water, as a royal dish is sodden in liquids. They place a wide copper utensil on the fire and fill half of it with water. When the water boils they place the pot with the meat in cold water above the boiling water. Thus is the meat cooked.²⁸⁰ and *mevushal*. This dish is better than one prepared close to the fire. I the writer²⁸¹ add to the words of this scholar what I heard from his very own mouth.²⁸² *Bashel* (sodden)²⁸³. is an adjective²⁸⁴ infinitive *bashel* (cf. *le-vashel*, to cook), as the infinitive form is vocalized with a *pattach* and has a *dagesh* in the *shin* (compare the *pi’el* infinitive *dabber*). following the paradigm of *kaved* (heavy) and *zaken* (old). The term *bashel* ²⁸⁵. here is similar,²⁸⁶ and *zaken*. as its *bet* ²⁸⁷ of *bashel* in the infinitive (see note 284) but like the *kof* of *kaved* and the *zayin* of *zaken*. is vocalized with a *kamatz* and its *shin*²⁸⁸ of *bashel* in the infinitive (see note 284) but like the *bet* of *kaved* and the *kof* of *zaken*. has no *dagesh. Bashel* is not an infinitive²⁸⁹ like *kabbed* (promote) in *for I will promote thee* (Num. 22:17) or *hakkeh* (smite) in *thou shalt surely smite* (Deut. 13:16), as the infinitive is not joined to a word unless it is a perfect or an imperfect. Compare, *dabber yedabber* (speak well) (Ex. 4:14),²⁹⁰ is an infinitive, *yedabber* an imperfect. *Dabber yedabber* (speak well) literally means speak, he will speak. and *hakdesh hikdashti* (I verily dedicate) (Jud. 17:3).²⁹¹ is an infinitive, *hikdashti* a perfect. *Hakdesh hikdashti* (I verily dedicate) literally means dedicate, I dedicated. However, the infinitive is never joined with the *po’el* or *pa’ul*. ²⁹², as *mevushal* is a *pu’al* participle. Hence the term *bashel* in *bashel mevushal* cannot be an infinitive. Thus *bashel* (sodden) is similar to *kaved* (heavy).²⁹³ is. Its feminine form is *beshelah*, as in *the shoulder…when it is sodden* (beshelah) (Num. 6:19). Do not ask what need Scripture had to use the two terms *bashel* and *mevushal*.²⁹⁴ As the scholar²⁹⁵ pointed out,²⁹⁶ there are two soddenings, one of which is²⁹⁷ the placing of the utensil with the meat in the midst of the boiling water. The plural of *bashel mevushal* is *beshelim mevushalim*. Compare, *chakhamim mechukkamim* (exceeding wise) in *But they are exceeding wise* (Prov. 30:24). The singular form is *chakham mechukkam*. Compare, *barukh u-mevorakh* (exceedingly blessed). There is a difference in nuance from a grammatical standpoint between *chakham* (a wise man) and *mechukkam* (one who has become wise).²⁹⁸ to the plural form of *chakham mechukkam. Chakham* means a wise man. *Mechukkam* means one who has been made wise (taught) by others. See I.E. on Prov. 30:24, “*Mechukkamim:* God gave them the wisdom to do this.” There is, as the scholar explained,²⁹⁹ a similar difference between *bashel* (sodden)³⁰⁰ and *mevushal* (sodden).³⁰¹, boiled, boiled in water. The difference between *bashel* and *mevushal* is explained by I.E. in his opening comment on this verse.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:15:1)


**שבעת ימים.** טעם מצות תאכלו, זכר לאכילתם בצאתכם ממצרים, כי לא צוה שיאכלו מצות רק הנאכלים עם הפסח לפני חצות לילה, רק שבעת ימים צוה לאכול מצות להיות זכר לאשר קרה לכם בצאתכם ממצרים כי שם כתוב כי לא חמץ, ואלו היו מניחים המצריים שיתמהמהו מעט היו מחמיצין עיסתם, והשבעת ימים בצאתם מצות אכלו עד שטבע פרעה ביום השביעי, כי הענן היה מוליכם יומם ולילה, ולא היו מתעכבים בחנותם עכוב רב, וככה כתוב על הפסח, שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות לחם עני (דבר' טז ג), והנה הזכיר על הפסח שבעת ימים תאכל מצות חיוב על דרך הפשט והעד למען תזכור את יום צאתך (שם) ובעבור זה כתוב, כל מחמצת לא תאכלו בכל מושבותיכם תאכלו מצות (פ' כ) חיוב בארץ ישראל ובחוצה לארץ:


SEVEN DAYS SHALL YE EAT UNLEAVENED BREAD. The reason for *shall ye eat unleavened bread* is to recall the *matzot* eaten when they left Egypt. They were not previously commanded to eat unleavened bread save for that which is to be eaten with the paschal lamb before midnight.³¹⁸(v. 8). However, God now commanded that they eat unleavened bread for seven days³¹⁹ in memory of what happened to them when they left Egypt, as it is written there,³²⁰ *for it was not leavened* (Ex. 12:39). Had the Egyptians permitted them to tarry a bit, they would have leavened their dough. They ate unleavened bread for seven days until Pharaoh was drowned on the seventh day. The heavenly cloud led them day and night and they did not tarry very long even when they camped.³²¹ It is similarly written when discussing the paschal lamb,³²² *seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction* (Deut. 16:3). Now according to its plain meaning, the text *Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread* is stating an obligation.³²³ 120a. Also see Rashi on this verse. *That thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life* (Deut. 16:3) is proof of this.³²⁴ for seven days an obligation, since both are written in one verse. It is because of this³²⁵ that Scripture states, *Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread* (Ex. 12:20), as the latter³²⁶ is an obligation within the Land of Israel and outside of the Land of Israel.

³²² Which is to be eaten in all generations.
³²³ Contra the Talmudic opinion that the obligation to eat unleavened bread is limited to the first night of Passover. See Pesachim
³²⁴ Just as remembering the Exodus all the days is an obligation, so is eating matzot
³²⁵ It is because Scripture connected the obligation to eat unleavened bread with the paschal lamb, which is only offered in the Land of Israel.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:15:2)


ואחר שקבלה היתה ביד ישראל שיחלו לשחוט את הפסח בנטות השמש לצד מערב וכתוב לא תשחט על חמץ דם זבחי (לד כה) על כן דרשו רז"ל אך חלק, ודע כי כלוי מעשה אינו מעשה והנה פירוש ויכל אלהים ביום השביעי (ברא' ב ב) כאשר נכנס היום השביעי כבר כלתה מלאכתו וככה ביום הראשון תשביתו שאור מבתיכם, בהכנס היום הראשון כבר נשבת כל השאור מהבתים והנה תחלת יום ראשון סוף יום י"ד בערב, ככתוב מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי, והנה פירוש זה, כי שבעת ימים שלמים הם מיום י"ד לחדש בערב שהוא סוף יום י"ד, עד יום הכ"א לחדש בערב, ועוד אדבר על זה:


[HOWBEIT THE FIRST DAY YE SHALL PUT AWAY LEAVEN OUT OF YOUR HOUSES.] Now since Israel had a tradition of commencing the slaughter of the paschal lamb when the sun started going down towards the west, and it is written, *Thou shalt not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread* (Ex. 34:25), the rabbis of blessed memory interpreted the word *ach* (howbeit) to mean a part of.³²⁷ 5a. It is a general principle in Talmudic exegesis that *ach* and *rak* imply limitations. Thus *ach* divides the day, indicating that the putting away of the leaven is to take place in the middle of the day. According to the rabbis, *ach ba-yom ha-rishon tashbitu se’or mi-batekhem* (howbeit the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses) is to be rendered: At the middle of the day which is before the festival of unleavened bread ye shall put away leaven out of your houses. Mark the fact that ceasing an act is not an act. The meaning of *And on the seventh day God finished* (Gen. 2:2) is: when the seventh day started God had already finished his work.³²⁸ Similarly, the meaning of *the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses* is: when the first day starts, all leaven shall already have been removed from the houses. Now *the first day* starts at the end of the fourteenth day at even, as it is written, *from the first day until the seventh day*. The meaning of the phrase³²⁹, etc. then is that the seven full days³³⁰ are from the fourteenth day of the month at even, which is the end of the fourteenth day, until the twenty-first day at even. I will yet speak concerning this.

³²⁸ See I.E. on Gen. 2:2.
³²⁹ Howbeit on the first day

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:16:2)


כל מלאכה. בכל המועדים חוץ מיום השבת ויום הכפורים אין כתוב בהם כל מלאכה רק בפסח לבדו אמר, והתנה להוציא אוכל נפש, ובכל מקום בין בפסח בין בעצרת בין ביום הזכרון וחג הסוכות היה אוחז דרך קצרה לומר כל מלאכה לא תעשו, רק במקום אחד בפסח לא תעשו כל מלאכה על דרך שהזכיר תחלה:


NO MANNER OF WORK. We do not find the phrase *kol melakhah* (no manner of work) stated with regard to any of the festivals,³³² (ye shall do no manner of servile work). See Lev. 23:8, 21, 25, 35; 36. Also see Num. 28:18, 26, 29:1, 12, 35. with the exception of the Sabbath and the Day of Atonement.³³³ (ye shall do no manner of work). See Ex. 20:10; Lev. 23:3, 28. Also see Num. 29:7. However, the phrase³³⁴. is employed with regard to Passover³³⁵ with the proviso that *that which every man must eat* is permitted.³³⁶ In all other places, be it Passover,³³⁷ Sha’vu’ot,³³⁸ the Day of Memorial,³³⁹. See Lev. 23.25; Num. 29:1. or the festival of Sukkot,³⁴⁰ Scripture employs the abridged form and states, *ye shall do no manner of servile*³⁴¹ (no manner of servile work) and not *kol melakhah* (no manner of work) with regard to the festivals. Our text follows *Vat. Ebr*. 38. The printed editions read, *kol melakhah*. This is obviously a scribal error. *work*.³⁴². 38. The printed text read: No work shall be done. It is I.E.’s contention that *ye shall do no manner of servile work* is short for: ye shall do no manner of work save that which every man may eat, as *okhel nefesh* (that which every man must eat) is not considered *melekhet avodah* (servile work). Only in one place³⁴³ with regard to Passover is it stated that you shall do no manner of work under the first stated conditions.³⁴⁴.

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:19:1)


**שאור.** שהוא מחמיץ, והוא הידוע, ואחר כן אמר כל אוכל מחמצת, כל דבר שֶיֵחְמָץ ודע כי מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי, אינו דבק בקרוב אליו שהוא ונכרתה רק עם אוכל מחמצת כמו למלוך שלמה על ישראל (מ"א ו א'), אמר יפת, כי יש אות שמושכת עצמה ואחרת עמה אחורנית כמי אדם פטדה וברקת (למטה כה יז) שהטעם אדם ופטדה וברקת, וככה מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי:


LEAVEN. *Se’or* (leaven) refers to something which induces leavening. The substance is well known.³⁵¹. Scripture then goes on to say, *for whosoever eateth anything which is leavened* (machmetzet).³⁵² refers to anything which is leavened. Scripture first prohibits keeping anything which induces leavening (*se’or*) in one’s home on Passover. It then prohibits eating on Passover anything which is leavened. Note that *from the first day until the seventh day* (v. 15) is not connected to what is adjacent, i.e., to *shall be cut off*³⁵³, etc., does not follow *shall be cut off*. but rather is connected to³⁵⁴ to *from the first day*, etc., and read verse 15 as if written: For whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel. *for whosoever eateth leavened bread*.³⁵⁵ It is similar to *of Solomon’s reign over Israel* (I Kings 6:1).³⁵⁶ Yefet says that some letters refer both to the word in which they are placed and to a word previously written, as in *odem pitdah u-vareket* (carnelian, topaz, and smaragd) (Ex. 28:17), which is to be interpreted as if written, *odem u-pitdah u-vareket* (carnelian, and topaz, and smaragd).³⁵⁷ (and) placed in front of *vareket* also governs *pitdah*. The same is true of *mi-yom ha-rishon ad yom ha-shevi’i* (from the first day until the seventh day).³⁵⁸ placed before *ha-rishon* also governs the word *yom* that precedes it. So too the *heh* placed before *ha-shevi’i* governs the word *yom* that precedes it. The verse is thus to be understood as if written: *me-ha-yom ha-rishon ad ha-yom ha-shevi’i*. Yefet comments thus for it is Hebrew style to place a *heh* in front of the noun when there is one in front of the adjective. Compare, *ha-har ha-tov* (that goodly hill country) (Deut. 3:25) (Filwarg). See also Vol. 1, p. 47, note 168.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:21:3)


אמר המדקדק כי ושחטו הפסח מהבנין הדגוש, ולא דבר נכונה, כי ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל (פ' ו) הוא מהבנין הקל, והשי"ן קמוץ כמשפט בעבור הנח הנעלם, רק ושחטו הפסח לשון צווי מהבנין הקל, ולא מצינו מזאת הגזרה בכל המקרא מהבנין הדגוש, והיה ראוי השי"ן להיות חירק תחתיה כמו משכו, רק בעבור אות הגרון שהוא אחריו נפתח השי"ן כמשפטם לעשות כך כמו בַחֲרו לכם (יהושע כד טו) ורבים ככה, על כן יהיה השי"ן בפתח גדול בלשון צווי ושניהם מבנין אחד:


[AND KILL THE PASSOVER LAMB.] The grammarian³⁶⁵.(Weiser). says that *ve-shachatu* (and kill) in *and kill the passover lamb* is a *pi’el*.³⁶⁶ imperative. Compare, *dabberu, hallelu* However, he spoke incorrectly. *Ve-shachatu* (shall kill it) in *and the whole congregation of Israel shall kill it* (v. 6) is a *kal*.³⁶⁷ It³⁶⁸ in verse 6. is properly vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath the *shin* because of the silent missing letter.³⁶⁹ (a silent missing letter) is always placed beneath the first letter in the *kal* perfect. I.E. refers to the *kamatz* as a silent missing letter because the *kamatz* vowel implies an *alef*. See I.E. on Ex. 2:4 and the notes thereto. However, *ve-shachatu* (and kill) in *and kill the passover lamb* is imperative in the *kal*. We do not find this root in the *pi’el* in any place in Scripture.³⁷⁰ in our verse cannot be a *pi’el*. The *shin* of *ve-shachatu*³⁷¹ should have been vocalized with a *chirik*,³⁷² as *miskhu* (draw)³⁷³ plural imperatives are vocalized with a *chirik* beneath their first letters. is. However, since the *shin* is followed by a guttural³⁷⁴. it was vocalized with a *pattach*, as is Hebrew practice. Compare, *bacharu* (choose) in *choose you* (Josh. 24:15).³⁷⁵, not *bicharu* because a guttural, a *chet*, follows the *bet*. There are many other similar instances.³⁷⁶. The *shin*³⁷⁷. is therefore vocalized with a long *pattach* in the imperative. Both words³⁷⁸ (vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath the *shin*) in verse 6 and *ve-shachatu* (vocalized with a *pattach* beneath the *shin*) in our verse. are from the same conjugation.³⁷⁹. However, *shachatu* in verse 6 is a perfect and *shachatu* in our verse is in the imperative.

מלת אגודת כמו חבורה, כמו ויהיו לאגדה אחד (ש"ב ב כה), ורבי מרינוס אמר, כי האל"ף נוסף והוא מגזרת גדוד, ואחרים אמרו כי האל"ף שרש, כמו וחשב אפודתו (למטה כח ה):


[A BUNCH OF.] The word *aguddat* means a bunch (of). Compare, *la-aggudah* (band) in *and became one band* (II Sam. 2:25). Rabbi Merinus says that the *alef* in *aguddah* is appended,³⁸¹ and mean the same. as *aguddah* comes from the same root as *gedud* (troop).³⁸². Hence the *alef* is appended. Others say that the *alef* in *aguddah* is a root letter³⁸³. like the *alef* in *afuddato* (skillfully woven)³⁸⁴ minus the pronominal suffix is *afuddah*. Thus *aguddah* follows the paradigm of *afuddah*. in *and the skillfully woven band* (Ex 28:6).

footnotes:
³⁸¹ Or superfluous. It is not a root letter and has no meaning, as the word could read gudah
³⁸² Gen. 49:19. Its root is gimel, dalet, dalet
³⁸³ Its root being alef, gimel, dalet
³⁸⁴ From the root alef, peh, dalet. Afuddato


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:22:3)


והגאון פי' האזוב בלשון ערבי זעת"ר, ובלשון לעז אוריגנ"ו, והוא עשב נכבד במיני מטעמים, וזה לא יתכן, כי הכתוב אמר על האזוב אשר יצא בקיר (מ"א ה יג), ולא ידעתי מהו, רק מדרך הסברא אינו עשב תקיף, כי הוא הפך הארז שהזכיר הפסוק:


[HYSSOP.] Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that *azov* (hyssop) is a plant known in Arabic as *zatr* and in the vernacular as oregano. It is an herb distinguished by various kinds of flavors. However, this interpretation is incorrect, for Scripture states, *even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall* (I Kings 5:13).³⁸⁵ I do not know the identity of the *azov*. However, logically speaking it is not a very mighty plant for it is the opposite of the cedar mentioned in Scripture.³⁸⁶.

footnotes:
³⁸⁵ The oregano plant does not grow out of walls.
³⁸⁶ I Kings 5:13 reads: And he spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall

ויש אומרים כי הפסח היו שוחטין אותו בסף השער, וטבלו האזוב בו ויגיעו אל המזוזת, כמו וימד סף השער (יחז' מ ו) אמות הספים (ישעי' ו), ואחרים אמרו כי הוא כלי ועליו היו שוחטים, כמו, משכב וספות (ש"ב יז כה):


[BASIN.] Some say that they slaughtered the paschal lamb in the threshold of the gate,³⁸⁷ (basin) means a threshold. and they dipped the hyssop into it and then touched the side-posts with the blood. They say that the word *saf* (basin) is similar in meaning to the word *saf* (threshold) in *and he measured the threshold* (saf) *of the gate* (Ezek. 40:6)³⁸⁸ and to *sippim* (thresholds)³⁸⁹ is the plural of *saf*. in *and the posts of the thresholds moved* (Is. 6:4).³⁹⁰ Others say that *saf* (basin) is similar to *sappot* (basins) in *brought beds, and basins* (II Sam. 17:28) and that *saf* is a vessel over which they slaughtered the paschal lamb.

### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:23:1)


**ולא יתן המשחית.** לא יניחנו, כמו "כי על כן לא נתתיך לנגוע אליה" (ברא' כ ו), והנה המשחית ברשותו, ואם יניחנו כאילו נתן לו רשות:


AND WILL NOT SUFFER. He will not suffer *the destroyer. Yitten* (will suffer)³⁹² literally means, will give. At times it has the meaning of will give permission. Rashi similarly interprets, “He will not give him the power to come” into your homes. here is similar in meaning to *netatikha* (suffered I thee) in *Therefore suffered I thee not* (Gen. 20:6). Now, the destroyer is under God’s power. If God allows him to come into their homes it is as if He gave him permission to do so.

### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:24:1)


**ושמרתם.** רבים חשבו, כי נתינת הדם על המשקוף ועל שתי המזוזת חיוב לדורות, בעבור כי "הדבר הזה" סמוך אל לקיחת האזוב וטבילתו, ועוד כי כתוב אחר כן, אשר פסח על בתי בני ישראל (פ' כז) ובדרך הסברא נכון היה לולי קבלת האמת הנגמרת, הנה הנכון שמלת "הדבר הזה" שב אל ושחטו הפסח, וטעם שאלת הבנים בראותם כל המשפחה חבורה אחת אוכלים שה תמים ראשו על כרעיו ועל קרבו, ועצם לא תשברו בו, ובן נכר ותושב וערל ושכיר לא יאכל בו ואין זה המנהג במועדים אחרים:


AND YE SHALL OBSERVE THIS THING. Many are of the opinion that the placing of the blood on the lintel and on the two side-posts is an obligation for all generations because *this thing*³⁹³. is connected to³⁹⁴ the taking of the hyssop and dipping it into the lamb’s blood. Furthermore, Scripture afterwards states, *for that he passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt* (v. 27).³⁹⁵ which will be asked by children in future generations (v. 26). *Prima facie*, the question pertains to the placing of the blood on the lintels and on the side-posts. This interpretation would be correct from a logical point of view were it not for the true tradition which states otherwise.³⁹⁶ The correct interpretation is that *this thing*³⁹⁷ refers to *and kill the passover lamb*.³⁹⁸ The meaning of the children’s question is,³⁹⁹ when your children will see their family in a group eating an entire lamb, whose bones one is prohibited to break, with its head, with its legs, and with the inwards thereof, unlike the custom on all other festivals, and from which a gentile, an uncircumcised one, a sojourner, and a hired servant may not eat, they will question you.⁴⁰⁰

³⁹⁷ What mean ye by this service? See note 395.
³⁹⁸ In verse 21, and not to the taking of the hyssop and dipping it into the lamb’s blood.

### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:25:1)


**והיה.** עתה פירש כי שחיטת הפסח תלויה בארץ, ואל יקשה עליך פסח הר סיני, כי מצוה עליונה היתה, ולא עשו פסח אחר במדבר כי בהר סיני היו עם הישוב וימצאו מצות, ובהיותם בארץ אשר לא עבר בה איש, אין להם רק המן לבדו:


AND IT SHALL COME TO PASS. Moses now explains that the slaughter of the paschal lamb is contingent upon dwelling in the Land of Israel. Do not be troubled by the Passover observed by Israelites at Mount Sinai.⁴⁰¹ That was a commandment from on high.⁴⁰² They did not observe another Passover in the desert. At Mount Sinai they were in an inhabited land and were thus able to find unleavened bread. However, when they were in a land that no man passed through⁴⁰³. Hence the only Passover they could have celebrated was the one at Sinai. they only had manna.

⁴⁰² To observe that particular Passover outside of Israel (Num. 9:5). Otherwise Israel would not have offered the paschal sacrifice.
⁴⁰³ Jeremiah’s description of the wilderness in which Israel journeyed on the way to the promised land (Jer. 2:6). I.E. borrows Jeremiah’s description because he wants to emphasize that Israel had no one to buy wheat from to bake matzot

### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:27:1)


**ואמרתם זבח פסח.** מצאנו פסוח והמליט (ישעי' לא ה), והטעם כמו חמלה, ובעבור שהשם חמל על בכורי ישראל בעבור דם השה, נקרא השה פסח, כמו ושחטו הפסח (פ' כא), והגאון אמר שהוא מגזרת פסח כי הפסח ישען על רגלו התמימה, והמשחית כן עשה שהשחית בכורי בית המצרים, ופסח על בית שכנו העברי ולא השחיתו, וכמוהו, עד מתי אתם פוסחים (מ"א יה כא):


THAT YE SHALL SAY: IT IS THE SACRIFICE OF THE LORD’S PASSOVER. The word *pesach* (passover) is to be rendered pity, as we find, *paso’ach ve-himlit* (He will pity it and He will rescue it) (Is. 31:5).⁴⁰⁵ The lamb is termed *pesach* (passover), as in *and kill the passover* (pesach) (v. 21), because God had pity on the first-born of Israel because of the blood of the lamb. However, Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the word *pesach* is derived from the word *pi’se’ach* (limp), since a lame person supports himself on his healthy leg.⁴⁰⁶, a hopper or skipper. The destroyer acted in a similar manner. He exterminated the first-born in the Egyptian home and passed over⁴⁰⁷ the home of his Hebrew neighbor and did not destroy him. The term *posechim* (hopping) in *How long will you keep hopping between two opinions* (I Kings 18:20)⁴⁰⁸ is similar.

### Verse 31

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:31:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:31:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:31:1)


**ויקרא.** מדרך הסברא, כי משה ואהרן לא היו בליל ט"ו בארץ רעמסס עם ישראל, רק במצרים שהיתה מקום המלוכה שהיה שם פרעה, והנה יצאו הם מפתח ביתם במצות השם בחצי הלילה, ונתן להם רשות פרעה שילכו ישראל לעבודת השם, והנה הלך משה עם עבדי פרעה לרעמסס להוציא ישראל, וידוע היום כי יש בין מצרים הישנה שיש שם אוצרות יוסף ידועים עד היום, ובין רעמסס ששה פרסאות, והנה החלו לצאת בבקר, והוא עת עלות עמוד השחר, שיחל להראות אור השמש בעבים והנה יש בין תחלת זה הרגע, עד עת זרוח השמש שעה ישרה ושליש שעה, והנה יש לנו בקר והחשך גדול כמו, ותשכב מרגלותיו עד הבקר (רות ג יד) ושם כתיב בטרם יכיר איש את רעהו, והנה היו מישראל שיצאו בתחלת עמוד השחר ועודנו לילה בדרך התורה עד זרוח השמש, ואלה היו קרובים אל מצרים, והאחרים שהם רחוקים יצאו בו ביום, כי קהל רב היה, ויותר יש מתחלת רעמסס עד סופה משמונה פרסאות על כן כתוב, "הוציאך ה' אלהיך ממצרים לילה" (דבר' טז א) וכתוב אחר "היום אתם יוצאים" (למטה יג ד), ועוד, ובנ"י יוצאים ביד רמה (במדבר לג ג) וכתוב שם, ומצרים מקברים (שם שם ד), וביום יקברו, וכבר פירשתי:


AND HE CALLED. Logically speaking Moses and Aaron were not in the land of Rameses with the Israelites on the night of the fifteenth. On the contrary, they were in that part of Egypt in which was the royal seat where Pharaoh lived.⁴¹³ Now Moses and Aaron left the doors of their homes at midnight⁴¹⁴ in accordance with God’s dictate.⁴¹⁵, which pictures Moses and Aaron as staying in their homes until the morning and Pharaoh going around the land of Egypt asking, “Where does Moses dwell? Where does Aaron dwell?” According to the *Mekhilta*, when Pharaoh found Moses and Aaron he said to them, “*Rise up, get you forth*,” etc. Moses responded, “We are warned not to go out except in broad daylight as it is written, *And none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning*” (v. 22). After Pharaoh gave the Israelites permission to go and worship God, Moses went with the servants of Pharaoh to Rameses to bring Israel out of Egypt. It is common knowledge in our time that there are six Persian miles⁴¹⁶ between ancient Egypt, where Joseph’s treasures are known to be until this very day, and Rameses. Now the Israelites began to leave Egypt in the morning,⁴¹⁷ namely, at the break of dawn when the light of the sun is seen in the clouds. There is a full hour and a third between the moment that dawn breaks and sunrise. We find that it can be very dark and still be morning. Thus Scripture states, *And she*⁴¹⁸ *lay down at his feet*⁴¹⁹ *till the morning* (Ruth 3:14), and then adds, *before one could discern another*.⁴²⁰ Now some Israelites exited Egypt at the break of dawn when, from the Torah’s standpoint, it is still night until sunrise.⁴²¹ This group was close to Egypt. Another group who were further from Egypt exited that very day.⁴²² The Israelites constituted a very large congregation.⁴²³ It is more than eight Persian miles from one end of Rameses to another.⁴²⁴ Scripture therefore states in one place, *the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night*⁴²⁵ (Deut. 16:1), and elsewhere reads, *This day ye go forth*⁴²⁶ (Ex. 13:4). It is further stated, *the children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians* (Num. 33:3),⁴²⁷ and it is there recorded, *while the Egyptians were burying them that the Lord had smitten*. Now the Egyptians buried their dead during the day. I have thus explained the meaning of morning.⁴²⁸

⁴¹⁶ A Persian mile is, 8000 cubits, or approximately 2 1/2 miles.
⁴¹⁷ They were not allowed to leave their homes till this time (v. 22).
⁴¹⁸ Ruth.
⁴¹⁹ Boaz’s feet.
⁴²⁰ We thus see that when morning begins people still cannot recognize each other because it is yet dark.
⁴²¹ According to I.E. when the Torah speaks of day it means after sunrise.
⁴²² That is, after sunrise.
⁴²³ That is why it took so long for all of them to leave.

AND THEY DESPOILED. We do not find the root *nun, tzadi, lamed* ⁴³⁵ (and they despoiled). I.E. literally reads: we do not find the root of *hatzalah* in the *kal*. in the *kal*. They⁴³⁶ and the *hifil*. are both transitive verbs because there is no difference in meaning between *va-yenatzelu* (and they despoiled)⁴³⁷. and *va-yatzel* (hath taken away)⁴³⁸ from the root *nun, tzadi, lamed*. in *Thus God hath taken away* (Gen. 31:9) except that in the *hifil* the object⁴³⁹ (va-yatzel) *the cattle*. is mentioned and in the *pi’el* it is omitted.⁴⁴⁰ (va-yenatzelu) *the Egyptians*. ### Verse 37

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:37:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:37:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:37:1)


**ויסעו.** היו הסמ"ך ראוי להדגש בהתבלע הנו"ן כמו ויגשו (ברא' יט ט) ויתנו (שם לה ד), אולי בא כן להקל על הלשון:


AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED. The *samekh* in the word *va-yisu* (journeyed)⁴⁴¹. should have received a *dagesh* to compensate for the missing *nun*,⁴⁴² in *va-yisu*. A missing first root letter is compensated for by placing a *dagesh* in the second stem letter. as the *gimel* in *va-yiggeshu* (and drew near)⁴⁴³. In *va-yiggeshu* the *nun* drops out and is compensated for by a *dagesh* in the *gimel*. (Gen. 44:18) and the *tav* in *va-yittenu* (and they gave)⁴⁴⁴. (Gen. 35:4) do. It is possible that the *dagesh* was omitted to simplify enunciation.

### Verse 40

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:40:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:40:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/12:40:1)


**ומושב בני ישראל.** חשבונות רבים יש במקרא לא ידענו למי הם סמוכים, והנה אזכיר מקצתם ויהי מקץ ארבעים שנה ויאמר אבשלום (ש"ב טו ז), ואבשלום לא היה בן ארבעים שנה, גם לא נשלמה מלכות בית דוד, ומפרשים אמרו כי זה חשבון במצרים. אחר שאר הישיבות שישבו גרים מיום שבת הארון בקרית יערים, וכתוב ויהי בשלשים שנה (יחז' א א), י"א בן שלשים שנה נתנבא וי"א ליובל, וי"א מציאת ספר תורה שמצא חלקיהו הכהן, ואני לא ידעתי, כי הם סברות בלא יסוד ומשענת, וכתוב, בעוד ששים וחמש שנה (ישעי' ז ח), וזו הנבואה היתה בימי אחז, ומלכותו היתה שש עשרה שנה, ובשנת שש לחזקיהו בנו גלתה שומרון, ע"כ הוצרכו המפרשים לומר כי תחלת ששים וחמש שנה, מיום שנבא עמוס, וישראל גלה יגלה מעל אדמתו (עמוס ז יא), ואחרים אמרו משנת הרעש, וכאשר חפשנו שנות שבא ישראל בימי יוסף ואחיו, הנה לא יגיעו מספר ימי הכתוב כי אין ספק כי קהת מיורדי מצרים היה, ונחשוב כי הוליד עמרם בנו בסוף ימיו, גם עמרם הוליד משה בסוף ימיו, והנה מספר חייהם מאתים ושבעים שנה, ומשה בן שמונים שנה בצאת ישראל ממצרים, והנה הכל ג' מאות ונו"ן שנה, הנה חסרו לנו שמונים והזקנים הוסיפו אשר ישבו במצרים ובשאר ארצות. כי, ועבדום וענו אותם ארבע מאות שנה (ברא' טו יג) אינו דבק עם וענו, רק עם יהיה זרעך וכמוהו רבים, ובפרשה הזאת "מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי" (פ' טו), ואחר שמצאנו כתוב, שהשם אמר לאברהם בין הבתרים כי גר יהיה זרעך ארבע מאות שנה, ידענו כי חשבון מושב בני ישראל, תלוי בקץ אברהם, והוצרך בעל סדר עולם לומר, כי אחר שבא אברהם לארץ כנען שב לחרן, והוצרכו המפרשים לומר, כי נבואת אני ה' אשר הוצאתיך מאור כשדים (ברא' טו ז) איננה דבקה עם הפרשה הנזכרת אבל אחר זה נאמרה, ואין צורך לכל זה, רק חשבון ד' מאות שנה הוא מיום שנולד יצחק, ואלה השלשים שנה הנוספים, מספרם מיום שיצא אברהם מארץ מולדתו מאור כשדים, ובא עם אביו אל חרן כאשר כתוב ויבואו עד חרן וישבו שם (שם יא לא), ואברהם ישב עם אביו בחרן חמש שנים, ובא אל ארץ כנען, והוא בן חמש ושבעים שנה, ולא שב אל חרן, והנה כאשר נולד יצחק תמו שלשים שנה שיצא אברהם מארצו, כי הוא העיקר, כי לו נתנה ארץ הכנעני, ויהיה פסוק אני ה' אשר הוצאתיך מאור כשדים (שם טו ז) דבק עם כל הפרשה למעלה ולמטה, והנה פי' ומושב בני ישראל אשר ישבו במצרים, שהיו גרים שם, גם אבותיהם היו גרים, ככתוב כמעט וגרים בה (תה' קה יב), ואברהם אמר גר ותושב אנכי עמכם (ברא' כג ד):


NOW THE TIME THAT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL DWELT IN EGYPT WAS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS. There are many calculations⁴⁵⁴ in Scripture whose point of departure is unknown to us. I will now mention a few of them. *And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said unto the king* (II Sam. 15:7). Now Absalom was not then forty years old.⁴⁵⁵ Furthermore, King David’s reign was not yet over.⁴⁵⁶ The commentaries tell us that the point of departure for this calculation is *from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim* (I Sam. 7:2). It is stated, *Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year* (Ezek. 1:1). Some say that Ezekiel was thirty years old when he began to prophesy.⁴⁵⁷ refers to the thirtieth year of Ezekiel’s life. Others say that the reference is to the thirtieth year of the jubilee.⁴⁵⁸ Other say that its point of departure is the finding of the Torah which was discovered by Hilkiah the priest.⁴⁵⁹ 26 and *Targum Jonathan*. However, I am uncertain, for they are opinions without foundation or support. It is written: *And within threescore and five years shall Ephraim*⁴⁶⁰. *be broken, that it be not a people* (Is. 7:8). The latter prophesy was uttered during the days of Ahaz, whose reign lasted for sixteen years. Samaria was exiled in the sixth year of his son Hezekiah’s reign.⁴⁶¹ The commentaries were therefore forced to say that the sixty-five years start from the day that Amos prophesied, *And Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land* (Amos 7:11). Others say that its point of departure is the earthquake.⁴⁶² Now when we investigated the years starting with the time that Israel came to Egypt in the days of Joseph and his brothers we found that they do not come to the number of years spoken of in Scripture.⁴⁶³ There is no doubt that Kehat⁴⁶⁴ was among those who descended to Egypt.⁴⁶⁵ Let us imagine that Kehat⁴⁶⁶ begot his son Amram at the end of his life and that Amram⁴⁶⁷ similarly begot Moses at the end of his life. Now the years of Kehat and Amram’s lives come to two hundred and seventy. Moses was eighty years old when the Israelites went out of Egypt.⁴⁶⁸ It all thus comes to three hundred and fifty years. We are missing eighty years. It is for this reason that the elders⁴⁶⁹ added, “dwelt in Egypt and other countries.”⁴⁷⁰ 9a. The *four hundred years* in *and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years* (Gen. 15:13) is not connected to *and they shall afflict them*⁴⁷¹ but rather to *thy seed shall be a stranger* (*Ibid.*).⁴⁷² There are many other such instances.⁴⁷³ We similarly find in our own chapter, *from the first day until the seventh day* (v. 15).⁴⁷⁴ Now we find it stated that God told Abraham at the covenant made “between the pieces,”⁴⁷⁵. See Gen. 15. *that thy seed shall be a stranger…four hundred years*. We know that the number of years that Israel dwelt in Egypt⁴⁷⁶ is contingent upon the “end,”⁴⁷⁷ which was told to Abraham.⁴⁷⁸ The author of the *Seder Olam*⁴⁷⁹ was compelled to say that after Abraham came to the land of Canaan he returned to Haran.⁴⁸⁰ explains that the number 430 refers to the time that passed from the “covenant between the pieces” (Gen. 15), and the number 400 refers to the time from the birth of Isaac. The accounting is as follows: Abraham was 70 years old when God made the “covenant between the pieces” with him and told him that his children would be strangers for 400 years (Gen. 15:13). Abraham then went to Haran and spent five years there, as it is written, *And Abraham was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran* (Gen. 12:4). Now Isaac was born when Abraham was 100 years old (Gen. 21:5). Abraham thus lived in Canaan for 30 years without a son. Exodus, as noted above, starts the count from the “covenant between the pieces.” Genesis starts the count with the birth of Isaac 30 years later. However, it must be pointed out that the *Seder Olam*’s accounting is based on a number of assumptions: a) That the covenant between the pieces occurred when Abraham was 70 years old. Scripture nowhere says so. b) That Abraham returned to Haran. Scripture does not say this either. Hence I.E. did not want to accept the *Seder Olam*’s calculations. The question thus remains how to reconcile the number of years mentioned in Exodus with those given in Genesis. The commentaries were forced to say that the prophecy *I am the Lord that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees* (Gen. 15:7) is not connected to the above-noted chapter⁴⁸¹ but was said later.⁴⁸². However, there is no need for all of this.⁴⁸³ Only the counting of the four hundred years is from the day that Isaac was born.⁴⁸⁴, for Scripture speaks there of *thy seed*. The additional thirty years start from the day that Abraham left Ur of the Chaldees, the land of his nativity, and came with his father to Haran, as it is written, *and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there* (Gen. 11: 31). Abraham lived in Haran with his father for five years.⁴⁸⁵ He came to the land of Canaan at the age of seventy-five and never returned to Haran. Now thirty years passed from the time that Abraham left Haran till the day Isaac was born. Abraham was the important one,⁴⁸⁶ and to him was the land of the Canaanite given. The verse *I am the Lord that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees* (Gen. 15:7) is connected to the entire chapter preceding⁴⁸⁷ and following it.⁴⁸⁸ The meaning of *Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in Egypt* is to be explained: they were strangers there, also their fathers were strangers, as it is written, *Yea, very few, and sojourners in it* (Ps. 105:12); and as Abraham said, I *am a stranger and a sojourner with you* (Gen. 23:4).

Now Scripture tells us that Abraham left Haran when he was 75 (Gen. 12:4). Therefore he spent five years in Haran. In his commentary on Genesis, I.E. implies that we cannot ascertain how many years Abraham spent in Haran. See I.E. on Gen. 12:1 and the notes thereto.
⁴⁸⁶ Hence the calculations in our verse begin with him.
⁴⁸⁷ Literally, above.
⁴⁸⁸ Literally, below. In other words, the words in the verse were said to Abraham at the “covenant of the pieces.”

**ליל שמורים הוא לה'.** על דרך הפשט בעבור שהזכיר ליל שמורים הוא לה', ובסוף שמורים לכל בני ישראל לדורותם, נראה כי הטעם בעבור שהשם שמרם, ולא יתן המשחית לבוא אל בתיהם לנגוף, צוה שיהיה זה הלילה שמורים לכל בני ישראל לדורותם, והטעם אכילת הפסח על משפטו, ומצות ומרורים בלילה הזה, ויש מפרשים אותו כטעם שומרי החומות (ש"ה ה ז) שלא ישנו רק יודו ויספרו גבורת השם בצאתם ממצרים, וככה רמזו חכמינו ז"ל, הגיע זמן קריאת שמע של שחרית (הגדה של פסח):


IT WAS A NIGHT OF WATCHING UNTO THE LORD. Since Scripture notes, *it was a night of watching unto the Lord*, and concludes by saying, *this same night is a night of watching unto the Lord for all the children of Israel throughout their generations*, the plain meaning of our verse appears to be: since God watched them and did not suffer the destroyer to come into their homes to plague them,⁴⁹¹. the Lord commanded that this night be *a night of watching*⁴⁹² means both watch and observe. Since God watched (*shamar*) Israel on this night, Israel must observe (*li-shemor*) God’s special laws this night. Hence *lel shimurim* (a night of watching) means a night of observance.*for all the children of Israel throughout their generations* through the eating of the paschal lamb according to its ordinance and the ingesting of unleavened bread and bitter herbs on this night. Others say that watching here has the same meaning as the word watching in *The watchers of the walls* (Cant. 5:7); its meaning is that they should not sleep on this night but should praise God and relate the might that the Lord displayed when they went out of Egypt.⁴⁹³ means a watch night. Our sages hinted at the latter meaning when they said, *The time for the reading of the morning shema has arrived*.⁴⁹⁴ 10.

Since Scripture mentioned *t*hat it was *a night of watching* (v. 42), the reference being to the night of the fifteenth wherein the paschal lamb is to be eaten, the *Torah* completes its explanation of the laws of the Passover⁴⁹⁵ that is to be observed in future generations. Now Scripture does not mention the lintel and the side-post. Neither does it mention that the lamb is to be eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs,⁴⁹⁶ as they were previously mentioned with regard to the Passover observed in Egypt. Its meaning⁴⁹⁷. thus is: you shall eat the Passover offering in the future as you ate it in Egypt. Scripture then added other commandments.⁴⁹⁸ However, the commandments with regard to the lintel and the side-post have nothing to do with the eating of the paschal lamb.⁴⁹⁹ Do you not see that at the beginning of the chapter (i.e., v. 43) it states, *there shall no alien eat thereof* (bo)?⁵⁰⁰ The meaning of *bo* (thereof) is, of it.⁵⁰¹ usually means in him or in it. Its usage in this context is correct in Hebrew⁵⁰² (he shall not eat of it), although from a very literal point of view it means he shall not eat in it. and also in Arabic.⁵⁰³ *Ve-hanotar ba-basar u-va-lechem* (and that which remaineth of the flesh and of the bread) (Lev. 8:32) is similar.⁵⁰⁴ means “of.” *Ba-basar* literally means in the meat and *ba-lechem* in the bread. However, in Lev. 8:32 *ba-basar u-va-lechem* are to be rendered of the flesh and of the bread.

AND THE LORD SPOKE. Scripture employs a short form,¹ for Moses stands in place of Israel.² is the same as saying, the Lord spoke unto Israel; i.e., the contents of this chapter pertained to Israel. However, Yefet says that Moses was commanded to verbally sanctify all first-born.³ The aforementioned is the reverse of *then the priest shall defile him* (Lev. 13:8);⁴. Both Moses and the priests perform their actions verbally. What I.E. means by the term “reverse” is that one makes someone unclean while the other makes one holy. the priest, being holy, defiles an individual by declaration.⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:2:1

**פטר.** פתיחת, כמו, ופטורי ציצים (מ"א ו יח) והטעם הבן שפתח תחלה הרחם, ומלת רחם זרה כי משפט לשון הקדש שיפתח האות שהוא לפני אות הגרון:


OPENETH. *Peter* (openeth) means the opening of. *Peter* is similar to *peture* (open) in *and open flowers* (I Kings 6:18). Its meaning is, the son who first opens the womb.⁶ literally means the opening of the womb, hence I.E.’s comment. The word *rechem* (womb) is irregular, as according to the rules of Hebrew grammar the letter preceding a guttural is vocalized with a *pattach*.⁷ in penultimately accented nouns. Compare, *nachal* (river), *lahav* (flame), and *na’ar* (youth) (Weiser). Hence our word should have been vocalized *racham* rather than *rechem*. Cf. Jud. 5:30.

### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:4:1)


**היום.** הזכיר בתחלה ולא יאכל חמץ, וככה תעשו לדורות, כמו שעשיתם ביום שיצאתם, וכאשר היה זה בזמן שהאביב נמצא ככה תעשו בכל שנה בעת המצא האביב בארץ ישראל, זהו האביב שעורה ופי' אביב כמו בִכּור, כי הוא מגזרת אב, שהוא כמו ראשון לאשר הוליד, או חכם לתלמיד שלמד, וכתוב כי השעורה אביב (למעלה ט לא), והעד שאמר בחג שבועות בכורי קציר חטים (למטה לד כב):


THIS DAY. Moses first mentions, *there shall be no leavened bread eaten*, its meaning being, do in future generations what you did on the day that you left Egypt.¹¹ As you left Egypt at the time when the first ears (*aviv*) are found,¹² (This day ye go forth in the month Abib). I.E. interprets this verse to mean: This day ye go forth in the month of fresh ears. so shall you do yearly in the future in the Land of Israel when the first ears come. The first ears refers to the first ears of barley. The word *aviv* (Abib) means the first that ripens.¹³ *Aviv* comes from the same root as *av* (father), which means first to the one whom one begets, or sage¹⁴. Cf. Jud. 17:10, *Dwell with me, and be unto me a father* (av) *and a priest*; and *Pirke Avot* (Ethics of the Fathers/Sages). to the student whom one teaches.¹⁵ means first in wisdom. Furthermore, it is written, *for the barley was in the ear* (aviv) (Ex. 9:31).¹⁶ refers to ears of barley. *Even of the first-fruits* (bikkure) *of wheat harvest* (Ex. 34:22),¹⁷, not *avivim*, for *aviv* refers to the first barley ears, which ripen about two months before the wheat does. which is written with regard to the festival of weeks,¹⁸ is proof of the above.¹⁹ means first.

**מצות.** הנה השבת הזהיר על גרך אשר בשעריך כי על זה התנאי יגור בשעריך שלא יעשה מלאכה לפני בשבת, וככה ביום הכפורים כי כן כתוב, וככה בפסח שלא יאכל חמץ במקום שהוא רשותו, וזהו טעם בכל גבולך:


UNLEAVENED BREAD. Similarly on the Day of Atonement, for it is so written.²³ (Lev. 23:32). The same applies to Passover, as a stranger is not permitted to eat leaven even on his own property. This is the meaning of *in all thy borders*.

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:8:1)


**בעבור זה.** אמר רבי מרינוס פי' בעבור זה, היה ראוי להיותו הפוך זה בעבור שעשה ה' לי, והביא רבים כמוהו לדעתו, ולפי דעתי, אין אחד מהם נכון, כי איך נהפוך דברי אלהים חיים, וטעם הפסוק הפך מחשבתו, כי אין אנו אוכלים מצות בעבור זה, רק פי' בעבור זה, בעבור זאת העבודה שהוא אכילת המצה, ולא יאכל חמץ שהוא תחלת המצוות שצוה לנו השם, עשה לנו השם אותות עד שהוציאנו ממצרים, והטעם לא הוציאנו ממצרים רק לעבדו ככתוב "בהוציאך את העם ממצרים תעבדון את האלהים על ההר הזה" (למעלה ג יב) וכתוב אשר הוצאתי אתכם מארץ מצרים להיות לכם לאלהים (במד' טו מא):


IT IS BECAUSE OF THAT. Rabbi Merinus says that *ba’avur zeh* (it is because of that) should have been written, *zeh ba’avur*; i.e., this is because of what the Lord did for me.²⁴) the Lord did for me when I came forth out of Egypt. Rabbi Merinus could find no sense in this. *Prima facie*, “because of this” refers to the eating of *matzah*. What meaning is there in: because of the eating of the *matzah*, the Lord did for me when I came forth out of Egypt? He thus interprets our verse to mean: It is because of that (*zeh ba’avur*) which the Lord did for me when I came out of Egypt that I eat *matzah* and abstain from leaven. He cited what in his opinion are many other such instances.²⁵, chap. 28. However, I do not think that he was right in even one instance. For how can we invert the words of the living God? The meaning of the verse is just the opposite of what he understands it to be, because we do not eat unleavened bread “because of this.”²⁶ is not to be interpreted as a reason for the eating of the matzah and abstaining from leaven. Its meaning rather is: it is because of this, i.e., it is because of this service, namely, the eating of unleavened bread and the abstention from leavened bread, which are the first of the precepts that God commanded us, that the Lord did signs for us and brought us out of Egypt.²⁷ Its meaning thus is: God took us out of Egypt only to serve Him, as it is written, *when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain* (Ex. 20:12). It is furthermore stated, *I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God*:²⁸ *I am the Lord your God* (Num. 15:41).

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:9:1)


**והיה לך.** יש חולקין על אבותינו הקדושים שאמר כי לאות ולזכרון, על דרך "כי לוית חן הם לראשך, וענקים לגרגרותיך" (משלי א ט), גם וקשרתם לאות על ידיך (דבר' ו ח) כמו "קשרם על לוח לבך תמיד" (משלי ו כא) גם, וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך (דבר' ו ט) כמו כתבם על לוח לבך (משלי ג ג) ומהו שיהיה לאות ולזכרון שיהיה שגור בפיך, כי ביד חזקה הוציאך ה' ממצרים, ואין זה דרך נכונה כי בתחלת הספר כתוב משלי שלמה, והנה כל מה שהזכיר הוא דרך משל, ואין כתוב בתורה שהוא דרך משל חלילה, רק הוא כמשמעו, על כן לא נוציאנו מיד פשוטו, כי בהיותו כמשמעו איננו מכחיש שקול הדעת כמו ומלתם את ערלת לבבכם (דבר' י טז) שנצטרך לתקנו לפי הדעת:


AND IT SHALL BE A SIGN UNTO THEE. There are those who oppose our holy patriarchs²⁹ refers to the phylacteries placed upon the hand and head. and say³⁰. This is obviously a scribal error. The correct reading is, *she-ameru*. that *for a sign…and for a memorial* is to be understood in the manner of *For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy head* (Prov. 1:9).³¹ They also say that *And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand* (Deut. 5:8) is like *Bind them continually upon thy heart, Tie them upon thy neck* (Prov. 6:21)³² and also that *And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house* (Deut. 6:9) is like *Write them upon the table of thy heart* (Prov. 3:3). They furthermore say that *it shall be for a sign…and for a memorial* means *for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought thee out of Egypt* shall drop from your lips.³³ However, this is incorrect, for at the beginning of the book of Proverbs it is stated, *The Proverbs of Solomon*. Thus whatever Solomon henceforth mentions is by way of parable. However, it is not, heaven forbid, written in the Torah that it is metaphoric. Hence it is to be taken only at face value. We thus will not interpret it except literally. It does not contradict reason if explained according to its plain meaning, like *Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart* (Deut. 10:16), which has to be interpreted according to the requirements of reason.³⁴

**שֶׁגֶר.** על משקל אֶרֶץ שלא ישתנה בסמיכה רק נמצאו מלות זרות ואלה הם, שְׁגַר אלפיך (דבר' ז יג) ובחֲדַר משכבך (למעלה ז כח), הֲבל הבלים (קהלת א ב), מספח חֲמָתְךְ (חבקוק ב טו) וסגור דְלְתךָ (ישעי' כו כ) לא מצאתי יותר:


COMING OF. *Sheger*⁴¹. (coming of) follows the paradigm of *eretz* (land of) whose vocalization does not change in the construct. However, a number of irregular cases⁴² whose vowels change to *sheva, pattach* in the construct. are found. They are: *shegar* (the increase of)⁴³, as in our verse. in *the increase of thy kine* (Deut. 7:13), *chadar* (chamber of)⁴⁴. in *and in the chamber of thy bed* (Ex. 7:28), *havel* (vanity of)⁴⁵. in *Vanity of vanities* (Eccles. 1:1), *hamatekha* (thy venom)⁴⁶. in *That puttest thy venom thereto* (Hab. 2:15), and *delatekha* (thy doors)⁴⁷. in *and shut the doors* (Is. 26:20). I have not found any additional instances.

AND EVERY FIRSTLING OF AN ASS. Which is unclean, *thou shalt redeem with a lamb*.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:13:2)


**וערפתו.** י"א תכתוב על ערפו קדש והאומר כזה, אומר אני שהוא חמור קשה עורף, כי הנה כתוב הוא יערוף מזבחותם (הושע י ב), וערפו שם את העגלה בנחל (דבר' כא ד) שהפירוש לכרות העורף כאשר פי' מעתיקי הדת, כי כל בכור שלא יקרב לגבי המזבח או לא יפדה חייב מיתה כי כל בכור מצרים אדם ובהמה מתו, כי ה' לא מלטם מן הגזרה שגזר על בכורי מצרים, רק שיהיו מוכנים לעבודתו, ולא היו לישראל בהמות טמאות כי אם החמורים לבדם ע"כ לא יפדה בכור מין אחר:


THOU SHALT BREAK ITS NECK. Some say that *va-arafto* (thou shalt break its neck) means thou shalt write the word holy on its neck.⁴⁸ means a neck. Hence *va-arafto* literally means: and you shall neck it. Hence the possibility of this interpretation. However, I say that anyone who says this is himself a stiff-necked ass. For behold it is written, *He will break down* (ya’arof) *their altars* (Hos. 10:2),⁴⁹ means to break. and *ve-arefu sham et ha-eglah ba-nachal* (and shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley) (Deut. 21:4), in which the meaning of *ve-arefu* is, as explained by the transmitters of the law, to cut off the neck.⁵⁰ All firstlings that are not brought up on the altar or are not redeemed are required to be killed, as all the first-born of Egypt both man and beast perished. God did not save them⁵¹ from the decree which he had issued on the first-born of the Egyptians except that they should be prepared for His service. The Israelites had no unclean animals except for asses. Therefore no other⁵² first-born⁵³ is to be redeemed.

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:14:1)


**והיה.** אמר ר' יהודה הלוי ז"ל, כי מחר חסר אלף והטעם מה שהוא אחר היום:


AND IT SHALL BE. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi of blessed memory says that the word *machar* (in time to come)⁵⁴ is missing an *alef*, its meaning being that which comes after today.⁵⁵ is short for *me’acher* (after). Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi interprets this way because “And it shall come to pass when thy son asketh thee tomorrow (*machar*),” etc., makes no sense in our context, whereas *And it shall come to pass when thy son asketh thee in time to come* (machar) does. Also see Rashi, “There are instances when *machar* means after some time.”

### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:15:1)


**ויהי.** החל לומר בחוזק יד הוציאנו, ושב לפרש מה היתה היד החזקה, והיא מכת הבכורים, כי על יד זה יצאו ממצרים, ולא על יד מכות הראשונות, וככה אמר המשורר, למכה מצרים בבכוריהם כי לעולם חסדו (תה' קלו י), ומשה תפס דרך קצרה, כי ידוע היה באמרו, ויהרוג ה' כל בכור והציל בכורינו ובכור בהמתינו, ועם זה ידבק על כן אני זובח ולא עם הריגת בכורים:


AND IT CAME TO PASS. Moses begins by saying, *By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt* (v. 14) and backtracks and explains that what the strength of hand refers to is the plague of the first-born. It was because of this plague, and not because of the first plagues, that Israel went out of Egypt. The poet similarly says, *To Him that smote Egypt in their first-born, For His mercy endureth for ever* (Ps. 136:10).⁵⁶ (Ps. 136:11). None of the other plagues are recalled in Ps. 136. Only this plague is mentioned, because it was the one that caused Pharaoh to permit Israel to leave Egypt. Moses wrote elliptically. When Moses said, *that the Lord slew all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beasts*, it was known⁵⁷ that God saved our first-born and the first-born of our cattle. It is to the latter,⁵⁸ not to the slaying of the first-born, that *therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the womb* is connected.

**ויהי בשלח.** וי"ו ולא נחם כפ"א רפה בלשון ישמעאל וידוע כי ממצרים עד ירושלים דרך פלשתים אינו מרחק רב, והוא כמו מהלך עשרה ימים בדרך הישרה, ולולי זה איך היו באים השבטים בחמוריהם עד מצרים אם היה הדרך רחוק' מאוד מה היה מספיק שיאכלו הם וחמוריהם, ובעלותם מביאים שבר לבתיהם:


AND IT CAME TO PASS WHEN PHARAOH HAD LET THE PEOPLE GO. The *vav* in *ve-lo nacham* (led them not) is like an unaspirated *fa* in the Arabic tongue.⁶⁸ prefixed to a word does not always mean and. Hence *ve-lo nacham* does not mean: and led them not, but may mean: that God led them not, or something similar. It is known that the distance between Egypt and Jerusalem by way of the land of the Philistines is not very great. It is about a ten-day journey by straight road. If this was not so, how did the tribes⁶⁹ come as far as Egypt upon their asses?⁷⁰ If the distance was very great how much would have been necessary for them and their asses to eat?⁷¹ Furthermore, upon returning they brought back food for their households.⁷²

**כי קרוב הוא.** א"ר משה אעפ"י שהוא קרוב וכמוהו לפי דעתי, כי עם קשה עורף הוא (למטה לד ט) רפאה נפשי כי חטאתי לך (תה' מא ה) כי רכב ברזל לו (יהושע יז יה) ולפי דעתי אין צורך, כי טעמו למה לא נחם אלהים דרך ארץ פלשתים בעבור שהוא קרוב, והנה נחם דרך רחוקה שלא יראו מלחמה, ויאמרו נתנה ראש ונשובה מצרימה:


ALTHOUGH THAT WAS NEAR. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that *ki karov hu* means *although that was near*.⁷³, which usually means “for” or “because,” has the meaning of “although” here. Rabbi Moses interprets thus, for *prima facie*, the word, “because” is out of place here, as God should have led them by the way of the Philistines because it was close. In my opinion, *ki am keshe oref hu* (for it is a stiff-necked people) (Ex. 34:9); *refa’ah nafshi ki chatati lakh* (Heal my soul; for I have sinned against Thee) (Ps. 41:5); and *ki rekhev barzel lo* (though they have chariots of iron) (Josh. 17:18) are similar.⁷⁴ in these verses is to be translated as although. Hence Ex. 34:9 is to be translated, *although it is a stiff-necked people*; and Ps. 41:5, *Heal my soul; although I have sinned against Thee*. However, I see no need for this interpretation,⁷⁵ here as although. for its meaning is: the reason God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines was that it was close.⁷⁶ is to be rendered, because it was close. God thus led them via a distant way so that they would not witness any war and say, *Let us make a captain, and let us return to Egypt* (Num. 14:4).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 13:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:18:1)


**וַיסב.** מפעלי כפל סבב, גם יבוא על משקל אחר וַיָסֶךְ בדלתים (איוב לח ה) וַיָגֶל את האבן (ברא' כט י) ולא תשמע לדברי האומרים ששרשו נסב:


LED THE PEOPLE ABOUT. *Va-yassev* (led about)⁸⁰ beneath the *yod*, a *tzere* beneath the *samekh*, and a *dagesh* in the *samekh*. is a verb⁸¹. that comes from a double root. Its stem is *samekh, bet, bet. Va-yassev* also has an alternative vocalization.⁸², with a *kamatz* beneath the *yod* and a *segol* beneath the *samekh*. For a double root in the *hifil* imperfect may be vocalized *pattach tzere*, as in *yassev*, or *kamatz segol*, as in *yasekh, yagel, yasev*. Compare, *va-yasekh* (shut up) in *Or who shut up* (Job 38:8)⁸³. and *va-yagel* (and rolled) in *and rolled the stone* (Gen. 29:10).⁸⁴. Pay no heed to those who say that the root of *va- yassev* is *nun, samekh, bet*.

ומלת המדבר. מושך עצמו ואחר עמו והוא דרך המדבר מדבר ים סוף, וכמוהו הארון הברית (יהושע ג יד) הארון ארון הברית, ועץ הדעת (ברא' ב ט) דעת טוב ורע, הספר המקנה (ירמיה לב יב) היין החמה (שם כה טו) וכמוהו רבים:


[THE WILDERNESS.] The word *ha-midbar* (the wilderness) is to be read as if written twice.⁸⁵. Now a definite article cannot be prefixed to a word in the construct. Hence I. E. argues that *ha-midbar yam suf* is short for *ha-midbar, midbar yam suf*. See Vol. 1, Foreword, p. XV, and I.E. on Gen. 2:9. (Jer. 32:12) and *ha-yayin ha-chemah* (the wine of fury) (Jer. 25:15).⁸⁹ is short for *ha-yayin, yen ha-chemah* (the wine, wine of fury). There are many other similar instances.

וסוף הוא שם מקום, וי"א שהוא מגזרת סוף דבר (קהלת יב יג), כי הוא סוף העולם, והוא ים אוקינוס כאשר כבר זכרתי וזאת טעות גדולה, כי הוא ים מזרחי כנגד מצרים וים ספרד גדול ממנו:

Others say that *suf* comes from the same root as *sof* (the end)⁹⁰ (Red Sea) is a variant of *yam sof* and means the Sea of the End, that is, the sea which lies at the end of the world. in *The end of the matter* (Eccles. 12:13). It is so called because it lies at the end of the world. The reference is to the Atlantic, which I have already mentioned.⁹¹ However, this is a major blunder, because the *yam suf* (Red Sea) lies in the east, opposite Egypt.⁹² The Spanish Sea⁹³ is larger than it.⁹⁴

**וחמושים.** י"א מלאים הון שיש להם כל צרכיהם והנה כתוב וגם צדה לא עשו להם (למעלה יב) ומה טעם להזכיר זה עתה. רק פירושו חגורי חומש למלחמה כמו חלוצים תעברו (דבר' ג יח) שפי' חגורי חלצים, והעד הנאמן ואתם תעברו חמושים (יהושע א יד) ובמקום אחר קראם חלוצים, כי מה טעם להוליך צדה לפני אחיהם, וטעם להזכיר הכתוב וחמושים במקום הזה, כי למעלה כתוב בראותם מלחמה כי ביד רמה יצאו בכלי מלחמה ולא כמו עבדים בורחים:


ARMED. Some say that *chamushim* (armed) means full of wealth, possessing all that they need. Now Scripture states, *neither had they prepared for themselves any victual* (Ex. 12:39).⁹⁵ Furthermore, what reason is there to mention this now?⁹⁶ The only meaning of *chamushim* is, girded with weapons for war. Compare, *chalutzim ta’avoru* (ye shall pass over armed) (Deut. 3:18), the meaning of which is: ye shall pass over with girded loins.⁹⁷ means loins. Therefore, *chalutzim ta’avoru* literally means: ye shall pass over with loins, i.e., with loins girded with weapons. The fact that Scripture in one place reads, *ve-attem ta’averu chamushim* (but ye shall pass over before your brethren armed) (Josh. 1:14) and in another place refers to the Israelites as *chalutzim* (Deut. 3:18) is true witness to the aforementioned.⁹⁸ means armed. What reason was there for them to carry food before their brethren?⁹⁹ means stocked with food then Josh. 1:14 tells us that the tribes of Dan and Reuben and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over the Jordan before the rest of Israel, carrying food. Now what conceivable reason was there for this? Food carriers or baggage follow behind troops. They do not precede them. The reason Scripture at this point notes *that the children of Israel went up armed* is that it is previously stated, *Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt* (v. 17).¹⁰⁰ For¹⁰¹ the Israelites went out *with a high hand* (Ex. 14:8), with weapons of war and not like fleeing slaves.
