###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:31:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:31:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:31:2)


יש אומרים כי כזרע גד לבן כוסברתא, ונקרא בלשון ערבי כסביר וי"א חרדל, ואנכי לא ידעתי כי אין לו חבר במקרא רק בדבר המן וככה צפיחית, והגאון אמר כי הוא רקיק מצות והנה כשיאכל כאשר ירד הוא כצפיחית בדבש, ואם יבושל יהיה טעמו כלשד השמן, אלה השנים מטעמים הראנו הכתוב:


[AND IT WAS LIKE CORIANDER SEED, WHITE.] Some say that *gad* (coriander) refers to *kosbarta,* in Arabic, *kusbar.* Others say that it means mustard. However, I do not know, as it is not found in any other context save in reference to the manna. The same is the case with the word *tzappichat* (wafers), which Saadiah Gaon says means an unleavened wafer. Now when the manna was eaten as it was when it came down, it had the taste of a wafer made with honey. However, when cooked it had the taste of a cake baked in oil (Num. 11:8). Scripture mentions these two delicacies.¹⁶⁰

footnotes:
¹⁶⁰ However, when prepared in other ways it had other tastes.



### Verse 32

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:32:1)


**ויאמר.** זאת הפרשה ראויה היתה להכתב אחר שנעשה המשכן רק נכתבה במקום הזה לספר זה הנס שעומד המן לדורות והנה משה אמר כן לישראל על כן אמר אשר האכלתי אתכם:


AND MOSES SAID. This chapter should have followed the account of the construction of the Tabernacle.¹⁶¹ (the jar of manna) *up before the Lord.* This implies that the Tabernacle was in existence, as *before the Lord* means before the ark (v. 33). Hence the command to set aside a jar of manna was not given when the manna stated to fall but later, after the construction of the Tabernacle. It was placed here to relate the miracle of the manna¹⁶² lasting for generations.¹⁶³ Now Moses told this to Israel.¹⁶⁴ He therefore said, *wherewith I fed you*.¹⁶⁵ our verse should read: that they may see the bread wherewith I fed them. Hence I.E. points out that when Moses spoke to Israel he used the second person. Thus our verse reads, I fed you.

¹⁶⁵ Our verse reads, that they may see the bread wherewith I fed you. Prima facie,

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:7:2)


**מסה ומריבה.** בעבור שני דברים הנזכרים, ומשפט לשון הקדש כאשר יזכיר שני דברים יחל לעולם מהשני שהוא הקרוב כמו ואתן ליצחק את יעקב ואת עשו (יהושע כד ד) ואח"כ ואתן לעשו (שם), וככה הזכיר תחלה מסה, ואחר כך מריבה, ושב לפרש קריאת מריבה על ריב בני ישראל עם משה, ופי' מסה על נסותם את ה', והנה פי' המסה "היש ה' בקרבנו" שיעשה כל צרכנו, וזאת הכת השניה הכעיסה ה' יותר מן הראשונה, ע"כ אמר לא תנסו את ה' אלהיכם כאשר נסיתם במסה (דבר' ו טז):


MASSAH AND MERIBAH. Because of the two reasons noted.²² It is the style of the Hebrew language to begin its comments with the second of two items when two particulars are listed,²³ as the second item is at hand. Compare, *And I gave unto Isaac Jacob and Esau* (Josh. 24:4), which is followed by *and I gave unto Esau* (*Ibid*.). Scripture similarly first mentions Massah and then Meribah and turns to explain that the name of the place was called Meribah *because of the striving of the children of Israel* with Moses. It then explains that the place was called Massah *because they tried the Lord.* Now “trial” refers to Israel’s asking, *Is the Lord among us* to provide for all of our needs? This second party angered God more than the first.²⁴ Scripture therefore says, *Ye shall not try the Lord your God, as ye tried Him in Massah* (Deut. 6:16).²⁵

footnotes:
²² In our verse Massah means trying and Meribah strife.
²³ Scripture first mentions Massah and then Meribah. It then goes on to first explain Meribah and then Massah.
²⁴ For the first complained because they were overpowered by thirst.
²⁵ The first party is not mentioned at all in this verse.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:11:1)


**והיה.** יש אומרים כי הרמת ידו כאשר במלחמה מי שבידו הנס, ואילו היה כן מרים אותו אהרן או חור או יעמידוהו במקום גבוה בהר שיראה עומד והנכון מה שאמרו קדמונינו:

Some say that Moses held his hand³³ up in a manner similar to one holding up a banner in war.³⁴ However, if this was the case then Aaron or Hur would have lifted the rod up or they would have placed it on a high place on the mountain so that the people would see it standing. The correct interpretation is the one offered by the ancient sages.³⁵ 3:8: “Now do the hands of Moses promote or hinder the battle! It is rather to teach you that when the Israelites directed their thoughts on high and subjected their hearts to their Father in heaven, they prevailed; and if not they were defeated.”

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:12:1

**וידי משה.** ידענו כי אין כח באדם להרים ידיו יום שלם, ואפילו שעות מועטות, ואף כי עד בא השמש, והנה הזכיר וידי משה כבדים יותר מידי שאר הזקנים, ע"כ לא היה יכול להרימם תמיד:

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:2)


וטעם וישימו שלא היה יכול לעמוד ושגבו מקומו:


[AND PUT IT.] Its meaning is, they strengthened his place³⁸ because he was not able to stand up.³⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:3)


ואהרן וחור עמדו, ואמר הכתוב כבדים על לשון זכרים, וככה מזה אחד ומזה אחד, וכמוהו והנה יד שלוחה אלי והנה בו מגלת ספר (יחז' ב ט):


AND AARON AND HUR. Stood. Scripture employs the masculine *kevedim* (heavy)⁴⁰. *Yad* (hand) is a feminine, hence I.E.’s comment. and similarly reads, *mi-zeh echad u-mi-zeh echad* (the one on the one side, and the other on the other side).⁴¹ refers to the hands. However, since *yad* is feminine Scripture should have read *mi-zot echad u-mi-zot echad.* *Ve-hinneh yad sheluchah elai, ve-hinneh vo megillat sefer* (behold, a hand was put forth unto me; and, lo, a roll of a book was therein) is similar (Ezek. 2:9).⁴² (therein) is masculine. However, *yad* is feminine. We thus see that Scripture occasionally combines feminine nouns with masculine pronouns or adjectives.

⁴⁰ Rather than the feminine kevedot
⁴¹ I.E. interprets our text as meaning: one was supporting this hand and one was supporting the other hand. In other words, mi-zeh
⁴² Vo


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:12:4)


**ויהי ידיו אמונה.** כל אחד מידיו כמו בנות צעדה (ברא' מט כב) וכמו וצדיקים ככפיר יבטח (משלי כח):


AND HIS HANDS WERE STEADY. Each one of his hands.⁴³ (his hands) is plural; *emunah* (steady) is singular. Hence *va-yehi yadav emunah* (and his hands were steady) means: and his hands was steady. I.E. holds that when a verb or an adjective in the plural governs or modifies a noun in the singular, the verb or adjective refers to each one within the plural. Hence, “and his hands was steady” means: and each one of his hands was steady. See Vol. 1, Foreword, p. xvii. The phrase is grammatically similar to *Its branches run over the wall* (Gen. 49:22)⁴⁴ (its branches) is plural; *tza’adah* (run) is singular. According to I.E., Gen. 49:22 should be translated: each one of its branches runs over the wall. See I.E. on Gen. 49:22 and the notes thereto. and *But the righteous*⁴⁵ (righteous) is plural; *kefir* (young lion) is singular. According to I.E., Prov. 28:1 should be translated: but each one of the righteous is secure as a young lion. *are secure as a young lion* (Prov. 28:1).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:12:5

ואמונה דבר עומד וקיים והוא שם דבר וי"א מגזרת ויהי אומן את הדסה (אסתר ב ז) כאלו אומנים הם שישאו ידיו:


STEADY. *Emunah* (steady) is a noun meaning something lasting and permanent.⁴⁶ Others say that *emunah* comes from the same root as the word *omen* (brought up)⁴⁷ means a person who raises a child. Cf. Num. 11:12; II Kings 10:1; Is. 49:2. in *And he brought up Hadassah* (Esth. 2:7). Aaron and Hur were like nursemaids who lifted up his hands.⁴⁸ (and his hands were steady) means: and his hands were nursed by nursemaids. For other interpretations and possible translations see Weiser and Krinsky.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 17:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/17:13:1)


**ויחלש** אין הפרש בין וַיַחֲלשׁ, ובין וַיֶחֱלָש (איוב יד י). כאשר טעם יִטְרֹף (תה' ז ג) כמו יִטְרָף (ברא' מט כז) כי תדר נדר (במד' ל ד) וַיִדַר יעקב (ברא' כה כ) בפתח רק זאת הגזרה כמלת שם, פעם יוצאת ופעם עומדת או יהיה גבר ימות ויחלש, וכבר חלש כדרך, וירם תולעים ויבאש (למעלה טז כ) ע"כ הזכיר גבר בעל גבורה:


AND JOSHUA DISCOMFITED AMALEK. There is no difference between *va-yachalosh*⁴⁹ (discomfited or weakened) and *va-yechelash*⁵⁰ Both words come from the root *chet, lamed, shin,* and may be used interchangeably. (weakened) (Job 14:10).⁵¹ Likewise, the word *yitrof*⁵² (tear) (Ps. 7:3) means the same as *yitraf*⁵³ (tears) (Gen. 49:27).⁵⁴ The same is the case with the words *tiddor* (voweth)⁵⁵ in *voweth a vow* (Num. 30:4) and *va-yiddar* (vowed),⁵⁶ which is vocalized with a *pattach* in *and Jacob vowed a vow* (Gen. 28:20). However, this root,⁵⁷ unlike *taraf* (tore) and *nadar* (vowed). like the word *shav* (returned), is sometimes transitive and sometimes intransitive.⁵⁸ Or,⁵⁹ in Job 14:20 is not only intransitive but also a pluperfect. *Vat. Ebr.* 38 reads: “Or *va-yechelash* means he weakened others… Scripture therefore employs *gever,* which indicates a mighty man.” Thus “or” introduces a new interpretation of the word *va-yechelash.* Whereas the previous interpretation believed it to be intransitive, this one believes it to be transitive. *va-yechelash* (weakened) in *a man* (gever) *dieth, and is weakened* (Job 14:10) means he was already weakened,⁶⁰ as *Vat. Ebr.* 38 does. The printed texts read: *u-khvar chalash acherim* (he has already weakened others). See above note. The point is *va-yechelash* is a pluperfect. Translated according to I.E., our verse should be interpreted: the mighty man (*gever*) who killed others dieth. Or, the mighty man weakened and dieth. like the word *va-yivash* (and rotted)⁶¹ in *and it bred worms, and rotted* (Ex. 16:20). Scripture therefore employs the term *gever* (man), which indicates a mighty man.⁶² is in contrast to *dieth.*

**וישמע יתרו.** הזכיר למעלה דבר עמלק כי לרפידים בא (למעלה יז ח), והיתה ראויה פרשת בחדש השלישי (יט א) להיותה כתובה אחר דבר עמלק, כי שם כתוב ויסעו מרפידים ויבאו מדבר סיני (שם פ' ב) א"כ למה נכנס דברי יתרו בין שתי הפרשיות והגאון אמר, כי יתרו בא אל מדבר סיני לפני מתן תורה, ולפי דעתי שלא בא רק בשנה השנית אחר שהוקם המשכן כי כתוב בפרשה עולה וזבחים לאלהים (למטה פ' יב) ולא הזכיר שבנה מזבח חדש ועוד כתיב והודעתי את חקי האלהים ואת תורותיו (פ' טז) והנה זה אחר מ"ת והעד הנאמן על דברי כי כן כתיב, אל המדבר אשר הוא חונה שם הר האלהים (פ' ה), ואמר משה לחובב שהוא יתרו, כאשר פירשתי בפרשת ואלה שמות כי חתן משה לא שב אל רעואל הקרוב אליו כי אם לחבב, כי כן כתוב מבני חבב חתן משה (שופ' ד יא) ומשה אמר לו, כי על כן ידעת חנתנו במדבר (במד' י לא) וידענו כי ישראל עמדו במדבר סיני כמו שנה והנה דברי משה יוכיחו שאמר בפרשת אלה הדברים "ה' אלהינו דבר אלינו בחרב לאמר, רב לכם שבת בהר הזה פנו וסעו לכם" (דבר' א ו ז), והנה זה הזמן היה קרוב למסעם, והוא אמר "ואמר אליכם בעת ההיא לאמר, לא אוכל לבדי שאת אתכם" (שם שם ט) כי השם הרבה אתכם והנכם היום ככוכבי השמים לרוב (שם פ' י), וטעם להזכיר זה להם, כי השם אמר ליעקב, הנני מפרך והרביתך ונתתיך לקהל עמים, ונתתי את הארץ הזאת לזרעך אחריך (ברא' מח ד) והנה הטעם כאשר ירבה זרעך אתן לו את הארץ, על כן אמר ה' אלהיכם הרבה אתכם, והגיע זמן שתירשו את הארץ, ובעבור שאתם רבים לא יכולתי לבדי שאת אתכם, והיצרכתי לתת עליכם שרי אלפים ושרי מאות, זאת היתה עצת יתרו שנתן לו ממחרת בואו למדבר סיני, על כן אמר משה לחבב שהוא יתרו, כמו שפירשנו נוסעים אנחנו (במד' י כט) והוא השיב, לא אלך כי אם אל ארצי ואל מולדתי אלך (שם שם ל), וזהו וישלח משה את חותנו וילך לו אל ארצו (פ' כז, ועתה אפרש למה נכנסה פרשת יתרו במקום הזה, בעבור שהזכיר למעלה הרעה שעשה עמלק לישראל הזכיר כנגדו הטובה שעשה יתרו לישראל וכתוב ויחד יתרו על כל הטובה, ונתן להם עצה טובה ונכונה למשה ולישראל, ומשה אמר לו, והיית לנו לעינים (במד' י לא), והטעם שהאיר עיניהם, ושאול אמר, ואתה עשית חסד עם כל בני ישראל (ש"א טו ו), ובעבור שכתוב למעלה "מלחמה לה' בעמלק" (יז טז) שישראל חייבים להלחם בו כאשר יניח השם להם, הזכיר דבר יתרו, כי הם היו עם גוי עמלק שיזכרו ישראל חסד אביהם, ולא יגעו בזרעו, והנה ראינו הרכבים, שהם בני יתרו היו עם בני ישראל בירושלים ובימי ירמיה, יונדב בן רכב (ירמיה לה יט), ויש פרשה אחרת דומה לזאת:


NOW JETHRO HEARD. Scripture notes above⁶ the incident of Amalek because Amalek came to Rephidim.⁷ Now the chapter that opens with the words *In the third month* (Ex. 19:1) should have followed the incident of Amalek,⁸ for Scripture states there, *And when they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the wilderness of Sinai* (Ex. 19:2).⁹ This being the case, why was the account of Jethro inserted between these two chapters?¹⁰ Saadiah Gaon says that Jethro came to the wilderness of Sinai before the giving of the Torah.¹¹ 116a), and of Rashi and Nahmanides. According to the Talmud, Jethro heard of the splitting of the sea and Israel’s war with Amalek at Rephidim. Hence the account of Jethro follows the war with Amalek. However, I believe that Jethro came to Sinai in the second year,¹² after the erection of the tabernacle.¹³ For the chapter¹⁴ speaks of *a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God* (v. 12),¹⁵ and it does not mention that he built a new altar.¹⁶ Furthermore, Scripture writes, *and I make them know the statutes of God, and His laws* (v. 16).¹⁷ Now this¹⁸ took place after the giving of the Torah.¹⁹ True proof that my words are correct is the fact that Scripture clearly states, *where he*²⁰ *was encamped, at the mount of God* (v. 5).²¹ (encamped) indicates that when Jethro came to Moses, Moses had been encamped there at Sinai for a long time. See I.E. on verse 19. Hence Jethro came after the giving of the Torah. Now Moses spoke to Hobab,²² (Num. 10:31). See further below. I.E. starts relating the aforementioned, then goes off on a tangent explaining who Hobab was, and then picks up the thread two sentences below. the latter being Jethro as I explained in the Torah portion *These Are The Names*.²³ For *Moses’ father-in-law*²⁴ does not refer to Reuel, which precedes the term father-in-law,²⁵ but refers to Hobab.²⁶ Scripture clearly states, *from the children of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses* (Jud. 4:11). Moses told Hobab, [*Leave us not, I pray thee*] *forasmuch as thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness* (Num. 10:31). Now we know that Israel camped around Sinai for about a year. Lo and behold, Moses’ very words prove this to be so. For Moses is quoted in the Torah portion, *These are the words* as saying, *The Lord our God spoke unto us in Horeb, saying: …turn you, and take your journey* (Deut. 1:6,7).²⁷ Now this was said close to their time of journey.²⁸ (Deut. 1:19) follows immediately. Moses continued, *And I spoke unto you at that time saying: I am not able to bear you myself alone* (Deut. 1:9); for *the Lord your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude* (Deut. 1:10). The reason Moses mentioned this to them was that God told Jacob, *Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a company of peoples; and will give this land to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession* (Gen. 48:4). Now the meaning of the latter is: when your seed increase I will give them the land. Moses therefore said, *the Lord your God hath multiplied you* and the time for you to inherit the land has come. However, since you are so numerous I was not able to carry you alone,²⁹ and I had to place over you captains of thousands and captains of hundreds.³⁰ Now this³¹ was the advice given to Moses by Jethro on the morrow following his coming to the wilderness of Sinai.³² Moses therefore said to Hobab, who, as we explained, is to be identified with Jethro, *We are journeying* (Num. 10:29).³³ Hobab responded, *I will not go; but I will depart to mine own land, and to my kindred* (Num. 10:30). This is what *And Moses let his father-in-law depart; and he went his way into his own land* (v. 27) refers to. I will now explain why the chapter dealing with Jethro was inserted here. It was placed here because Scripture had just mentioned the evil that Amalek did to Israel. The Torah wants to contrast it with the good that Jethro rendered Israel. Scripture notes, *And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the Lord had done to Israel* (v. 9) and that he gave proper and correct counsel to Moses and Israel. Moses told Jethro, *and thou shalt be to us instead of eyes* (Num. 10:31), meaning that he enlightened their eyes.³⁴ (and thou shalt be) as a perfect. He renders Num. 10:31 as: and you were to us instead of eyes; i.e., you enlightened us with your council. See I.E. on Num. 10:31 where he quotes this interpretation and prefaces it with the phrase, “many say.” King Saul similarly said,³⁵ *for ye showed kindness to all the children of Israel* (I Sam. 15:6).³⁶ because the good that Jethro had done accrued to the benefit of his descendants. See Kimchi on I Sam. 15:6. Now because Scripture states in the preceding chapter, *the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation* (Ex. 17:16), namely, that when God gives Israel rest they are obligated to wage war against Amalek, the Torah mentions the account of Jethro. For the descendants of Jethro lived in proximity to the nation of Amalek,³⁷ 38 reads: should they ever be found together with Amalek. It reads, *k i im* rather than *ki hem.* and the Torah wants Israel to remember the kindness that Jethro demonstrated so that they do not harm his seed. Thus we find the Rechabites, who were descended from Jethro, living among the children of Israel in Jerusalem. We find Jonadab the son of Rechab³⁸ in the time of Jeremiah (Jer. 35:19).³⁹ There is another chapter similar to the one above.⁴⁰

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:3:1)


**ואת.** דע כי אנשי לשון הקדש שומרים הפעלים במתכנתם בכל הבנינים, ואינם חוששים לשמור שמות בני אדם על כן אל תתמה שאמר גרשום בעבור שגר שם כי הנה קין (ברא' ד א) בעבור קניתי, ואינו נכון בדקדוק, וקשה מזה נח (שם ה כט) מגזרת ינחמנו ופעם יהפכו השם כמו חושים (שם מו כג) הוא שיחם (במד' כו מב), ונקרא יעבץ (דה"א ד ט) בעבור שילדתהו אמו בעוצב, גם יחסרו אות ממנו כמו מעכה הוא מיכה, והפך זה יוב (ברא' מו יג) הוא ישוב (במד' כו כד), ורבים אמרו כי כן שמואל (ש"א א כ) מגזרת שאלתיהו והישר בעיני כי שורק תחת חולם כמו תֹחוּ (ש"א א א) תיח (דה"א ו יט) וצוף (ש"א א א) וצופַי (דה"א ו יא) נון (למטה לג יא) ונון (דה"א ז כז), והנה שמואל מגזרת שמו אל, וקראתי אמו בשם אל, כי נתנו לה כאשר שאלה, ואל תתמה איך יקרא שם אדם בשם אל, כי הנה כמוהו צורי שדי (במד' ז לו) ורבים ככה, ולפי דעתי כי כן שם המזבח שבנה משה ה' נסי (למעלה יז טו) וככה שם המשיח ה' צדקנו (ירמיה כג ו), והגאון אמר כי השם דבק עם מלת יקראו ושם המשיח הוא צדקנו, והנה הוא מטעם בעל הטעמים ששם טרחא במלת יקראו כי הפרש גדול יש בין ויקרא בשם ה' (ברא' יב ח) הכתוב באברהם שהטרחא במלת ויקרא ובין ויקרא בשם ה' (למטה לד ה) הכתוב בספר משה כאשר אפרש במקומו:


AND. Note that those who speak the holy tongue preserve the verbal forms in all conjugations.⁵⁰ However, they are not careful to do so with proper nouns.⁵¹ Therefore do not be amazed that Moses called his son *Gershom* because he lived (*gar*) there (*sham*).⁵² I.E. explains the name *Gershom* as being a combination of *gar* and *sham.* However, in this case Moses should have named his son *Garsham* (Krinsky). We thus see that the Hebrews did not follow strict grammatical rules when coining proper nouns. For look, *kayin* (Cain) was so called because Eve said, *kaniti* (I have gotten) (Gen. 4:1). However, this is grammatically incorrect.⁵³ comes from the root *kof, nun, heh. Kayin* comes from the root *kof, vav, nun.* The name Noah, which Scripture derives from *yenachamenu* (shall comfort us) (Gen. 5:28),⁵⁴ is even more difficult.⁵⁵) comes from the root *nun, vav, chet.* If Noah were derived from *yenachamenu,* then he should have been called Menachem. See I.E. on 5:29. Scripture at times inverts a name. Thus *Hushim* (Gen. 46:23) and *Shuham* (Num. 26:42) are one and the same. *Yabetz* (Jabez)⁵⁶ was so called because his mother bore him in pain (*otzev*).⁵⁷ Thus the root of *otzev* is inverted in the name *Yabetz.* Sometimes a letter is dropped in a name, as in the case of Maacah⁵⁸ See II Chron. 11:21. which is a variant of Micah.⁵⁹ See Chron. II 13:2, where her name is given as Micaiah. Micah is a short form of Micaiah. I.E. apparently quoted from memory. Scripture drops the *ayin* the second time the name is mentioned. The reverse is true of *Yov* (Iob) (Gen. 46:13), which is the same as *Yashuv*⁶⁰ (Jashub) (Num. 26:24). Many say it is the same⁶¹ with *Shemu’el* (Samuel), which⁶² is derived from *she’iltihu* (I have asked him) (I Sam. 1:20).⁶³ is *shin, alef, lamed.* However, in my opinion a *shuruk* has been substituted here⁶⁴ for a *cholam,* as in the case of *Tohu*⁶⁵ (I Sam. 1:1) and *Toah*⁶⁶ is spelled with a *cholam.* Both refer to the same person. (I Chron. 6:19); *Zuph*⁶⁷ (I Sam. 1:1) and *Zophai*⁶⁸ Both refer to the same person. (I Chron. 6:11); *Nun*⁶⁹ (Ex. 33:11) and *Non*⁷⁰ Both refer to the same person. (I Chron. 7:26). Now *Shemu’el* (Samuel) comes from *shemo el* (his name is God).⁷¹ as the plain meaning of I Sam. 1:20 seems to imply. Samuel’s mother called him by God’s name because the Lord answered her request.⁷² Do not be amazed that a human being should be called by God’s name, for, observe, we find this to be the case with the name *Zurishaddai*⁷³ (Num. 7:36). There are many other similar instances.⁷⁴ In my opinion the altar which Moses built was similarly called *Adonai-nissi* (the Lord is my banner) (Ex. 17:15).⁷⁵ Likewise, the name of the Messiah will be called *Adonai-tzidkenu* (the Lord is our righteousness) (Jer. 23:6). However, Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that God’s name is connected to the word *yikre’o* (shall call him) and the name of the Messiah will be *tzidkenu* (our righteousness).⁷⁶ I.E. renders this clause: and this is the name whereby he shall be called: *Adonai-tzidkenu* (The Lord is our righteousness). Saadiah disagrees. He places a comma after the word *Adonai,* and translates: and this is the name whereby he shall be called by the Lord: *Tzidkenu* (Our Righteousness). Now its correct interpretation is in keeping with the opinion of the master of the cantillical notes,⁷⁷ who placed a *tircha*⁷⁸ in the Ashkenazic tradition. in the word *yikre’o*.⁷⁹ The *tippekha* is similar to a comma. Thus contra Saadiah, *yikre’o* is not to be connected to Adonai, and the clause is to be read as I.E. reads it. For there is a great difference between *va-yikra be-shem Adonai* (and called upon the name of the Lord) (Gen. 12:8), written in connection with Abraham with a *tircha* beneath the word *va-yikra*,⁸⁰ The latter is to be translated: And he, Abraham, proclaimed the name of the Lord. and *vayikra ve-shem Adonai* (and proclaimed the name of the Lord) (Ex. 34:5)⁸¹ The latter is to be rendered: And He (the Lord) proclaimed the name, Lord. See I.E. on Ex. 35:4. which is written in the Book of Moses⁸² i.e., in the story of Moses (Krinsky). as I will explain in its place.⁸³

**וישתחו.** דקדוק וישתחו קשה, ידענו כי שרשו מבעלי הה"א באחרונה, והנה הוי"ו במקום ה"א, כוי"ו "שלו הייתי" (איוב טז יב) שאמר ממנו לא שלותי (שם ג כו), והנה כאשר אמרו לשון יחיד וישתחו, היה ראוי להיות וישתחוה כי התי"ו מבנין התפעל כמו, והאיש משתאה לה (ברא' כד כא), כי משפט אותיות השיניים אם היה אחד מהם פ"א הפועל, והיה האות אשר לפניהם תי"ו התפעל, והנה בעבור שהחליפו הה"א בוי"ו במלת וישתחו הניחו וי"ו הראשון שאינו סימן לשון רבים תחת ה"א השרש והעלימו הוי"ו ואמר וישתחו, ובעבור היות הוי"ו בסוף המלה סימן לשון רבים כאשר הוא נעלם, כמו למה תתראו (ברא' מב א), והנה היה נראה מלת וישתחו בהעלם הוי"ו שהוא סימן לשון רבים ע"כ הוצרכה להיות המלה מלעיל להפריש בינה ובין מנהגם בלשון רבים:


AND BOWED DOWN. *Va-yishtachu* (and bowed down) is grammatically difficult.⁹⁶ 38 reads: “*Va-yishtachu* (he bowed) and also *estachaveh* (I will bow) are grammatically difficult.” That is, the entire paradigm is difficult, for its root is *shin, chet, heh* and it is spelled with a *vav*. *Va-yishtachu* is especially difficult in that the *heh* drops out and it is irregularly vocalized. We know that it comes from a root ending in a *heh*.⁹⁷ The *vav* in *va-yishtachu*⁹⁸ is in place of a *heh*,⁹⁹ like the *vav* of *shalev* (at ease)¹⁰⁰ However, a *vav* has been substituted for a *heh.* in *I was at ease* (Job 16:12), from whose root we get the word *shalavti* (at ease) in *I was not at ease* (Job 3:26). Now the term *va-yishtachaveh*¹⁰¹ ends *vav, heh,* while I.E.’s point is that the word should really have no *vav* at all. See note 96. Filwarg suggests two possible emendations: one, *va-yishtacheh,* the other, *va-yishtachev.* In the former, I.E. is explaining that if a *vav* had not been substituted for a *heh,* the word would have been *va-yishtacheh.* For the latter is the way third person *hitpa’el*’s are vocalized. If we emend to *va-yishtachev,* then I.E. is merely explaining why the word is vocalized *va-yishtachu* when, as noted above, according to Hebrew grammar the word should have been vocalized *va-yishtachev.* The error in transcription probably arose from the fact that the normally used word for “and he bowed” is *va-yishtachaveh.* See Filwarg and Krinsky. should have been employed in the singular,¹⁰² rather than *va-yishtachu,* for the *tav*¹⁰³ is a sign of the *hitpa’el* conjugation. It is like the *tav* in *mishta’eh* (steadfastly)¹⁰⁴ of the *hitpa’el* conjugation. in *And the man looked steadfastly on her* (Gen. 24:21). For the rule relating to the dentals¹⁰⁵ or *zayin.* states that if the first letter of a root before which the *tav* of the *hitpa’el* conjugation is placed¹⁰⁶ of the *hitpa’el* conjugation precedes the root. Compare *hitkatev,* *hityashev,* etc. is a dental, then¹⁰⁷ [the tav is placed after the first root letter].¹⁰⁸ the *tav* follows rather than precedes the *shin.* Now because the *heh* has been changed into a *vav* in *va-yishtachu* Hebrew allows the first *vav,*¹⁰⁹ (and they bowed) (Filwarg). which is not a plural suffix, to remain in place of the root *heh*¹¹⁰ and silences the *vav*.¹¹¹ I.E. refers to the *shuruk* as a silent *vav.* Hence the word reads *va-yishtachu.*¹¹² For other interpretations see Krinsky and Weiser. Now a *vav* at the end of a word is the sign of the plural suffix when silent as in *titra’u* (look one upon the other) in *Why do ye look one upon the other* (Gen. 42:1). Thus the word *va-yishtachu,* ending in a silent *vav,* would appear to be in the plural. *Va-yishtachu* was therefore penultimately accented¹¹³ to differentiate between it and the customary way of vocalizing plurals.¹¹⁴ is penultimately accented to indicate that it is not a plural.

**התלאה.** מגזרת ונלאו מצרים (למעלה ז יח) והתי"ו נוסף והטעם צרה שילאה אדם לסבלה או להגידה, והטעם על רדיפת מצרים בים, וביאת עמלק, וצמאו, ומכולם הצילם ה':


THE TRAVAIL. *Tela’ah* (travail) comes from the same root as *ve-nilu* (shall loathe)¹¹⁸ According to I.E. *ve-nilu* means unable. See I.E. on Ex. 7:18. in *and the Egyptians shall loathe* (Ex. 7:18). The *tav* is superfluous.¹¹⁹ Its meaning is, an affliction which a person is unable to bear or verbalize. It refers to Egypt’s pursuit of Israel at the sea, the war with Amalek, and the thirst and hunger which the congregation suffered. God delivered them from all of these.

**ויחד.** מגזרת חדוה, והיה ראוי להיותו על משקל וַיִפְתְּ בסתר לבי (איוב לא כז) וַיִשְׁבְּ ממנו שבי (במד' כא א) רק נפתח החי"ת בעבור שהוא מן אות הגרון, ונשאר הדל"ת דגוש כאשר היה, ולא אדע בכל המקרא אות דגוש בסוף המלה, רק אם היה בג"ד כפ"ת שיתחברו שני שואין שהם בסוף כמו וַיִשְׁבְּ ממנו (שם) וַיֵשְׁתְּ מן היין (ברא' ט, כא), רק עם אחד מהמלכים לא מצאנוהו דגוש רק פתח והם שנים "וַיִחַדְ יתרו" ואל יִחַד בימי שנה (איוב ג ו):


AND JETHRO REJOICED. *Va-yichad* (rejoiced) comes from the same root as the word *chedvah* (rejoicing).¹²⁰ The meaning of *va-yichad* thus is, and he rejoiced. It should have been vocalized like the word *va-yift* (enticed) in *And my heart hath been secretly enticed* (Job 31:27) and *va-yishb* (and took captive) in *and took some of them captive* (Num. 21:1).¹²¹ is *peh, tav, heh,* and that of *va-yishb* is *shin, bet, heh. Va-yift* is short for *va-yifteh* and *va-yishb* for *va-yishbeh;* that is, in words ending in a *heh,* the *heh* may be dropped in the imperfect. The latter is referred to as an abbreviated root. Now since the root of *va-yichad* is *chet, dalet heh, va-yichad* should have been vocalized *va-yichd.* However, the *chet* was vocalized with a *pattach*¹²² because it is a guttural, and the *dagesh*¹²³ in the long form, viz., *yechedeh.* remains in the *dalet*¹²⁴ has a *dagesh* in it. *Prima facie,* there is no reason for this *dagesh.* Hence I.E.’s comment. as it was. I am not aware of a letter having a *dagesh* at the end of a word in all of Scripture except in the case of a *bet, gimel, dalet, kaf, peh, tav* at the end of a word when two *sheva’im* come together,¹²⁵ as in the word *va-yishb* (and took captive)¹²⁶ beneath each of the last two letters, the *shin* and the *bet.* in *and took some of them captive* (Num. 21:1) and *va-yesht* (and he drank)¹²⁷ beneath each of the last two letters, the *shin* and the *tav*. in *And he drank of the wine* (Gen. 9:21). However, we never find a *dagesh* at the end of a word when preceded by a vowel¹²⁸ is not considered a vowel. except in the case of a *pattach.* In the latter case we find two such words namely, *va-yichad* (rejoiced) in *And Jethro rejoiced* and *yichad* (rejoice) in *Let it not rejoice among the days of the year* (Job 3:6).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:10:1)


**ויאמר יתרו ברוך ה'.** שים לבך לדקדק זאת המלה, דע כי לא יבוא פעול רק מפעלים היוצאים, ואם מצאת אותו שהוא על משקל פעול, הסתכל אם מצאת לו פועל שהוא יוצא הוא באמת פעול, ואם לא יהיה כן הוא תאר וככה אם היה על משקל פועל ואין לו פעול מהבנין בעצמו ומתוך הגזרה, גם הוא תאר ואינו פועל כלל כמו שמָרַ הפועל הוא שׁומֵר והפועל הוא עושר שָׁמור לבעליו (קהלת ה יב), והנה מצאנו הולך, עומד, יוצא, וכל אלה יראו פועלים, כי הם על מתכונת שומר, ובעבור שהגזרה מהפעלים העומדים, כי לא יאמר ממנו הלוך, עמוד, יצוא, והנה אין לנו פעול על כן אמר כי הולך הוא (במד' כב כב) תואר ואינו פועל, מצאנו עצום (שם שם ו) והוא יראה פעול, כי הוא על משקל שמור, וכאשר חפשנו זו הגזרה מצאנו וירבו ויעצמו (למעלה א ז) מהפעלים העומדים, כי היוצא יהיה מהבנין הנוסף וַיַעְצִמֵהו מצריו (תה' קה כד), והנה לא נוכל לומר עוצם, על משקל שומר, מענין עצמה (ישעי' מ כט) רק מענין אחר, ועוצם עיניו מראות ברע (שם לג טו), והנה מצאנו מלת ברוך על משקל שמור והנה חפשנו בכל המקרא, ולא מצאנו מזה הענין בבנין הקל רק מענין אחר, והוא וַיִברךְ על ברכיו (דה"ב ו יג) גם הוא פועל עומד לא יבוא ממנו פעול כלל, והנה מלת ברוך תואר כמו עצום מהבנין הקל, א"ר מרינוס, ברוך הוא תואר מבנין הדגוש, והיה הרי"ש ראוי להדגש ככל הגזרה כמו, ברך נבות (מ"א כא יג) והוא על משקל כדוב שַׁכּוּל (הושע יג ח) ולא דבר נכונה, כי כל תואר כמו שכול, וגבור, ושכור, לא ישתנו לסור הדגוש בסמיכת היחיד, או בלשון רבים, כמו ויהרג זכרי גבור אפרים (דה"ב כח ז) הוי גבורים (ישעי' ה כב), והנה עומד כנגדו בוא ברוך ה' (ברא' כד לא) ברוכים אתם לה' (תה' קטו טו):


AND JETHRO SAID: BLESSED BE THE LORD. Give your attention to the grammatical explanation of the word *barukh* (blessed). Note that the *pa’ul*¹²⁹ participle form. can only be formed from transitive verbs. If you find a verb following the *pa’ul* form, look around; if you find it has a transitive *po’el*¹³⁰ is the active *kal* participle form. form, then the word is a real *pa’ul.* However, if you do not find it to be so,¹³¹ then the word¹³² is an adjective.¹³³ Similarly, if a word is in the *po’el* form and its root does not come in the *pa’ul* in the same conjugation, then the word is also not a *po’el* but an adjective. For example, the *po’el* and *pa’ul* forms of *shamar* (kept) are *shomer* (keeps) and *shamur* (kept).¹³⁴ and *shamur* are true *po’el* and *pa’ul* forms. Compare, *shamur* in *riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt* (Eccles. 5:12). Now we encounter *holekh* (goes), *omed* (stands), *yotze* (goes out). All these words appear to be verbs in the *po’el,* for they follow the form of *shomer.* However, since these roots form intransitive verbs, for one cannot say *halukh* (wented), *amud* (stooded up), *yatzu* (wented out), these words do not come in the *pa’ul.* Therefore when Scripture uses the term *holekh* (went) in *because he went* (Num. 22:21), it employs an adjective, not a verb. We find [Scripture using] the word *atzum* (mighty). The word appears to be a *pa’ul* because it follows the paradigm of *shamur* (kept). However, when we investigated this root we found the word *va-ya’atzmu* (waxed mighty), in *and multiplied, and waxed exceedingly mighty* (Ex. 1:7), to be among the intransitive verbs. For its transitive form comes in the *hifil*¹³⁵ is in the *kal.* as in *va-ya’atzimehu* (and made them too mighty) in *and made them too mighty for their adversaries* (Ps. 105:24). Now we cannot say that *otzem* (strengthens) following the paradigm of *shomer* (keeps) means strength,¹³⁶ in the *kal* means waxed mighty, its *po’el* form does not mean waxes mighty but closes. In other words, the word *atzam* meaning strength has no *po’el* form. for in this case it has a different meaning, as in *otzem* (shutteth) in *And shutteth his eyes from looking upon evil* (Is. 33:15). Now we find the word *barukh,* which follows the paradigm of *shamur* (kept). We searched all of Scripture and we did not see this root¹³⁷ used with this meaning¹³⁸ in all of the *kal* conjugation.¹³⁹ in the *kal* means to kneel. It is only used with regard to a blessing in the *pa’ul* form. We found it used¹⁴⁰ only with another meaning, namely, to kneel, as in *va-yivrakh* (kneeled) in *and kneeled down upon his knees* (I Chron. 6:13), which¹⁴¹ is also intransitive and does not have a *pa’ul*¹⁴² form for kneeled because *barukh* means blessed. form. The word *barukh* (blessed) is thus like the word *atzum* (might), a *kal* adjective. Rabbi Merinus¹⁴³ says that *barukh* (blessed) is an adjective in the *pi’el.* Its *resh* should have received a *dagesh* like all other such roots,¹⁴⁴ receive a *dagesh* in their middle stem letters. When the middle root letter cannot receive a *dagesh,* the preceding letter is vocalized with a *tzere* in place of a *chirik.* such as *berekh* (curse)¹⁴⁵ rather than a *chirik* because the *resh* cannot receive a *dagesh.* In other words, the word for blessed should have been vocalized *berukh* rather than *barukh.* in *Naboth did curse* (I Kings 21:13). *Barukh* follows the paradigm of *shakkul* (bereaved)¹⁴⁶ It should be noted that *shakkul* is vocalized with a *pattach,* and *barukh* with a *kamatz.* The reason for the latter is that since the *resh* of *barukh* cannot receive a *dagesh*, the *pattach* preceding it is changed to a *kamatz.* in *as a bear that is bereaved of her whelps* (Hos. 13:8). However, Rabbi Merinus spoke incorrectly, for all adjectives such as *shakkul* (bereaved), *gibbor* (warrior), *shikkor* (drunk)¹⁴⁷ adjectives. do not undergo any change by having the vowel that precedes the *dagesh* change in the singular construct or in the plural.¹⁴⁸ does not change in the singular construct or in the plural. However, they do in the *kal.* Compare, *gibbor* (mighty man)¹⁴⁹ in *And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim* (II Chron. 28:7), and *gibborim*¹⁵⁰ preceding the *bet* with the *dagesh* in it does not change in *gibbor,* which is in the construct. Neither does it change in *gibborim,* which is the plural of *gibbor.* However, it does change in the *kal;* viz., *davar* becomes *devar i*n the construct and *devarim* in the plural. (mighty) in *Woe unto them that are mighty* (Is. 5:22). Now the word *berukh* (blessed of),¹⁵¹ in *Come in, thou blessed of the Lord* (Gen. 24:31) and *berukhim* (blessed) in, *Blessed be ye of the Lord* (Ps. 115:15), argue against Rabbi Merinus.¹⁵² We thus see that in the case of these two words the *kamatz* changes to a *sheva.* However, as noted above, this does not occur in the *pi’el* form. Hence *barukh* cannot be a *pi’el.* It has to be a *kal.*

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:10:2)


**אשר הציל אתכם.** אמר למשה ולאהרן שהיו שלוחים לשם, ועל ידם באו המכות לפרעה ולמצרים, על כן אמר מיד מצרים ומיד פרעה ואחר כן ברך השם אשר הציל את העם מתחת יד מצרים במצרים ובבקיעת ים סוף:


WHO HATH DELIVERED YOU. He said this¹⁵³ means: and Jethro said to Moses and Aaron. to Moses and Aaron, who were God’s messengers and through whom the plagues came upon Pharaoh and Egypt. Jethro therefore said, *out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh.* After this¹⁵⁴ he blessed the Lord, *who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians* in Egypt and at the splitting of the Red Sea.¹⁵⁵

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:11:2)


**וטעם כי בדבר.** בעבור הדבר שזדו המצרים על עם ישראל וכן הזכיר למעלה "ידעתי כי גדול ה' מכל האלהים" ה' שעושה דין על שהעבידו אותם בפרך וכן כתוב כי ידעת כי הזידו עליהם (נחמיה ט י) כאדם שיעשה בזדון רצונו, וכבר כתוב כי ידעתי את מכאוביו וארד להצילו מיד מצרים (למעלה ג ז ח):


[YEA, FOR THAT.] Because of the fact that the Egyptians dealt willfully with Israel.¹⁵⁷ (yea, for that) means: because of the fact, viz., the *bet* prefixed to *davar* means because. The *bet* usually means in. Hence I.E.’s comment. Jethro similarly, noted above, *I know that the Lord is greater than all gods* in that he punished the Egyptians because they made Israel work with rigor. It is similarly written, *Thou knewest that they dealt proudly* (hezidu) *against them* (Neh. 9:11) that is, they¹⁵⁸ behaved like a person who does whatever he wants to.¹⁵⁹ and *zadu* mean dealt willfully. Scripture already stated, *for I know their pains; and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians*¹⁶⁰ indicates that the Egyptians did what they wanted with Israel. (Ex. 3:7,8).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:13:3)


**מן הבקר עד הערב.** דע כי בקר האמת הוא כזרוח השמש, גם יקרא בקר בעלות עמוד השחר שיחל להראות אור בעבים, כמו שכבר זכרתי וזה הבקר הוא על דרך מקרה והערב האמיתי הוא בשקוע השמש, גם יקרא ערב על דרך מקרה עד עריבת האור וכן אמר דוד תזרח השמש יאספון (תה' קד כב) ואחריו כתיב, יצא אדם לפעלו ולעבודתו עדי ערב (שם פ' כג) על כן מערב עד ערב תשבתו שבתכם (ויקרא כג לב) והיה ראוי להיות מערב האמת עד ערב האמת רק חכמינו ז"ל הוסיפו מחול על הקדש, ואמרו כי יציאת יום השבת תהיה עד צאת הכוכבים, והנה ראוי להכניס השבת מן התורה מהשקע השמש, וכל חכמי התולדות וכל חכמי המזלות מודים, כי גבול היום מרגע היות עגולת השמש כנגד שטח הארץ בכל מקום, וזהו מעת צאתו עד בואו:


FROM THE MORNING UNTO THE EVENING. Note that true morning¹⁶³ begins with sunrise. The term morning is, as I have previously noted,¹⁶⁴ also applied to the breaking of dawn, when light begins to be seen in the clouds. In the latter instance the term is artificially used. Similarly, true evening begins when the sun sets. The term is also artificially applied up to the time that the light sets.¹⁶⁵ David similarly said, *The sun ariseth, they*¹⁶⁶ *slink away* (Ps. 104:22). Scripture then states, *Man goeth forth unto his work, And to his labor until the evening* (Ps. 104:23).¹⁶⁷ The psalm seems to describes man’s working hours from sunrise to sunset, for *erev* is antithetical to sunrise. We thus see that evening begins at sunset. It is therefore fitting to interpret *from even unto even, shall ye keep your sabbath* (Lev. 23:32) to mean: from the true evening to the true evening.¹⁶⁸ However, our sages of blessed memory “added from the weekday to the holy day”¹⁶⁹ and said that the Sabbath does not end until the stars come out.¹⁷⁰ 34b. It is thus fitting from the Torah’s point of view to start the Sabbath at sunset. All scientists and astronomers admit that the day’s boundary is¹⁷¹ the moment when the circle of the sun faces all over the area of the earth. This starts at sunrise and ends at sunset.

¹⁶⁶ The nocturnal creatures. We thus see that morning begins at sunrise.
¹⁶⁷ Erev.
¹⁶⁸ That is, from sunset to sunset.
¹⁶⁹ That is, the sages extended the holy day.
¹⁷⁰ See Sabbath
¹⁷¹ That is, day begins.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:14:2)


ורבינו שלמה אמר בעבור שמשה יושב לבדו וישראל נצבים ואין זה דרך מוסר ואין ספק כי מעלת משה גדולה לומר ככה כי הנה אהרן שהיה גדול לכל ישראל, והיה גדול בשנים ממשה הוא אומר לו בי אדני (במד' יב יא) ומשה עשה הדרך הנכונה, כי השופט יושב ובעלי הריב עומדים, וכן כתוב, ועמדו שני האנשים אשר להם הריב (דבר' יט יז) ולא אמר לו מדוע רק בעבור שהוא יושב למשפט לבדו ואין לו שופטים אחרים שיעזרוהו ואמר רבי מרינוס, כי מלת מדוע, כמו מַלֶכֶם (ישעיה ג טו) מַזֶה בידיך (למעלה ד ב) כי כל אחת שתי מלות וככה מלת מדוע מה דעתך לעשות ככה:


Rabbi Solomon¹⁷² says that Jethro reacted in this manner because Moses alone sat and Israel stood, the latter being improper.¹⁷³” There can be no doubt that Moses’ station was too great for Jethro to say this.¹⁷⁴ For behold, Aaron, who was a great man in the eyes of Israel and was older than Moses, said to Moses, *Oh my lord* (Num. 12:11). Moses acted in the proper manner, for the judge sits and the litigants stand. We thus read, *then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand* (Deut. 19:17). Jethro said, *why*¹⁷⁵ etc. to Moses for no reason other than that Moses was sitting alone and had no other judges to assist him. [WHY.] Rabbi Merinus says that the word *maddu’a* (why) is similar to *mallakhem* (what mean ye) (Is. 3:15) and to *mazzeh* (what is that) in *what is that in thy hand* (Ex. 4:2), each of which is a compound of two words.¹⁷⁶ being a compound of *mah* (what) and *zeh* (this) and *mallakhem* being a compound of *mah* (what) and *lakhem* (to you). The same is true of *maddu’a,* which means: what is in your mind that you do this?¹⁷⁷ is a compound of *ma* (what) and *du’a* (opinion), i.e., what is your opinion? *Du’a* is spelled *dalet, vav, ayin,* and is a variation of the root *yod, dalet, ayin,* meaning knowledge.

**ויאמר.** השיב משה אני עושה שני דברים, האחד כי יבא אלי העם לדרוש אלהים, והטעם לדרוש תורתו, והדבר השני, כי יהיה להם דבר בא אלי והשיב על האחרון תחלה ושפטתי בין איש ובין רעהו, והודעתי את חקי האלהים לדורש:


AND MOSES SAID. Moses answered, I do two things. One, *Because the people come unto me to inquire of God,* that is, to inquire of God’s law.¹⁷⁸ is short for, to inquire of God’s law. The other, *when they have a matter, it cometh unto me* (v. 16). Moses explained the second task first, namely, *and I judge between a man and his neighbor* (*ibid*.); and, he then said,¹⁷⁹ to one who inquires, *I make them know the statutes of God.*

### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:17:1)


**ויאמר לא טוב הדבר אשר אתה עושה.** בעיני, ונתן טעם לדבריו, והוא נבול תבול, מגזרת ועלהו לא יבול (תה' א ג) כאלה נובלת עליה (ישעי' א ל) כי הטעם שיפול מעצמו כנבול עלה דרך משל ומלת גם כמוה, גם כי כבד ממך הדבר:


AND…SAID…THE THING THAT THOU DOEST IS NOT GOOD. In my eyes. Jethro then explained himself, *Thou wilt surely wear away. Navol tibbol* (thou shalt surely wear away) comes from the same root as *yibbol* (wither)¹⁸⁰. *Navol* is an infinitive and *tibbol* an imperfect. The literal translation of *navol tibbol* is: wither you will wither; that is, you will collapse. in *And whose leaf doth not wither* (Ps. 1:3) and *novelet* (fadeth)¹⁸¹ in *For ye shall be as a terebinth whose leaf fadeth* (Is. 1:30). Its meaning is, you shall, as it were, drop like a withered leaf. The word *gam* (both)¹⁸² is to be prefaced also to *for the thing is too heavy for thee*.¹⁸³ is not a reason for what precedes it but an additional reason why Moses should not judge the people all by himself. For an alternate interpretation see Filwarg.

footnotes:
¹⁸⁰ The root, of which is nun, bet, lamed
¹⁸¹ Or withers.
¹⁸² Literally, also. Verse 18 reads: also thou, also this people.
¹⁸³ That is, for the thing is too heavy for thee



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:18:1)


**עשהו.** מלה זרה בדקדוק, ובאה על דרך לשמרהו, כי לא מצאנו ה"א נראית בגזרת עשה:


TO PERFORM IT. *Asohu* (to perform it) is grammatically inconsistent.¹⁸⁴ is *ayin, sin, heh.* When roots that end in a *heh* are combined with a pronoun, the *heh* changes to a *tav.* Hence our word should read *asoto* rather than *asohu.* It follows the form of *lishmerehu*¹⁸⁵ is a “whole,” i.e., a root that does not drop a letter. (to preserve him),¹⁸⁶ (preserve him) in Ps. 41:3. for we do not find the *heh* to be visible in the root *ayin, sin, heh*.¹⁸⁷ in this root is dropped when conjugated. Compare, *asiti, asita,* etc. Thus there is no reason why the root should follow the paradigm of a “whole” root when combined with a pronoun. Hence the grammatical inconsistency of *asohu.*

¹⁸⁵ Which, unlike the root of asohu,
¹⁸⁶ Cf. yishmerehu
¹⁸⁷ The heh

דע כי מלת אלהים הוא שם תואר כאשר פירשתי רק בעבור שידברו בה הרבה, יחשבו זה שם התואר כאילו הוא שם עצם, אלהים יראני בשוררי (תה' נט יא) בראשית ברא אלהים (ברא' א א) ורבים ככה, על כן שמוהו חכמינו ז"ל שם מן השמות שאינם ראוים להמחק:


[GOD.] Note that the term *Elohim* (God) is, as I have noted, an adjective.¹⁸⁸ It is only because the word is used often that this adjective is considered as if it were a proper noun. Examples of the latter are: *Elohim* (God) in *God will let me gaze upon my adversaries* (Ps. 59:11); *In the beginning God* (Elohim)*created the heaven and the earth* (Gen. 1:1), and many other instances. It is for this reason that our sages of blessed memory placed *Elohim* among the names that are not erasable.¹⁸⁹ is included among the latter. See chapter 4 of *Tractate Soferim.*

**וטעם ויהי אלהים עמך.** שהשם יעזרך אם תעשה ככה ואמר לו בסוף הדברים שיקח רשות מאת השם על העצה הזאת, וזהו אמרו וצוך אלהים ואין ספק כי כן עשה:


[AND GOD BE WITH THEE.] Its meaning is, God will help you if you act in this manner. At the close of his words, Jethro told Moses to ask permission of God to act in accordance with Jethro’s counsel. This is what Jethro meant by *and God command thee so* (v. 23). There is no doubt that Moses did so.¹⁹⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:19:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:19:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:19:5)

BEFORE GOD. From God’s side.¹⁹² The Biblical text reads, *mul ha-Elohim;* literally, before of God. I.E. apparently interprets it as: you will face the people from the same side as God faces them: that is, you will serve as God’s messenger to the people (Weiser). It is interesting to note that *Peshita* interprets similarly. It reads, “teaching the people from God.” However, the *mem* in I.E. often has the meaning of a *lamed.* Thus *mi-pe’at Elohim* might be interpreted as *li-fe’at Elohim;* that is, you will be the intermediary between the people and God (Krinsky). See Rashi. In this case, *mul ha-Elohim* means before God.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:20:1

**והזהרת.** הדרך השני שאמרת, אתה חייב ללמדם ולהורותם מספקות, כי טורח גדול הוא להודיע כל המעשה אשר יעשון וטעם והזהרת מן ולא נזהר (יחז' לג ה) וטעמו נשמר:


AND THOU SHALT TEACH THEM. As to the second thing you spoke of,¹⁹⁶ you are obligated to teach and instruct them only those things that they are uncertain of. For it takes great effort to teach all, *the work that they must do.* Now as to the meaning of *ve-hizharta* (and thou shalt teach): *ve-hizharta* comes from the same root as *nizhar* in *and took not warning* (Ezek. 33:5). *Nizhar* means took warning.¹⁹⁷ (and thou shalt teach) means: and thou shalt warn.

footnotes:
¹⁹⁶ That you are busy instructing the people.
¹⁹⁷ Hence ve-hizharta

והוא להזהירם על מצות עשה, ועל מצות לא תעשה הקשורים בלב שהוא העיקר כמו לאהבה השם ולדבקה בו, וליראה מפניו, וללכת אחריו ולמול ערלת הלב ולא ישנא אחיו, ולא יקום ולא יטור, וכן אמר משה בפיך ובלבבך לעשותו (דבר' ל יד) ורבים ככה:


[AND THOU SHALT TEACH THEM.] You shall warn them¹⁹⁹ to observe the positive and negative commandments that are tied to the heart,²⁰⁰ (duties of the heart) and wrote a work by that name. such as, to love God,²⁰¹ to cleave unto God,²⁰² to fear God,²⁰³ to walk after God,²⁰⁴ to circumcise the foreskin of the heart,²⁰⁵ not to hate one’s brother,²⁰⁶ not to take revenge,²⁰⁷ and not to bear a grudge.²⁰⁸ They are the most important commandments. Moses similarly said, [*But the word is very nigh unto thee*] *in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it* (Deut. 30:14).²⁰⁹ There many such precepts.

AND THE WORK THAT THEY MUST DO. The reference is to positive precepts which are observed by action. Most of them are not positive commandments that stand by themselves²¹⁰ acts of loving kindness. but serve as a reminder, such as the Sabbath,²¹¹ the Festivals,²¹² the redemption of the first-born,²¹³ loving the stranger,²¹⁴ ed. by J.H. Hertz, Soncino Press, London, 1967, p. 313. the fringes,²¹⁵ the *tefillin*,²¹⁶ the *mezuzah*,²¹⁷ See Deut. 6:4-8; 13:13-19. and also the prohibition against mixing linen and wool,²¹⁸ and many others.²¹⁹ I will explain them in their place.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:21:1)


**ואתה תחזה.** כבר הודעתיך כי אנשי לשון הקדש אינם שומרים המלות רק הטעמים על כן לא נחפש על חסר ומלא כאשר אפרש עוד והנה הזכיר יתרו אנשי חיל שיש להם כח לסבול טורח ולא יפחדו מהם והנה כנגד אנשי חיל אמר משה כשהוא מספר הדבר הבו לכם אנשים (דבר' א יג) כמו בחר לנו אנשים (למעלה יז ט) כלם אנשים (במד' יג ג):


MOREOVER THOU SHALT PROVIDE. I have already informed you that the speakers of Hebrew do not preserve exact wording. They only preserve meanings.²²⁰ Hence, as I will yet explain, we will not pay attention to whether the text is full or deficient.²²¹ Now when Moses recounted this incident,²²² in place of *able men*²²³ Literally, valiant men, mighty men. he said, *Get you…men* (Deut. 1:13).²²⁴ as in our verse. Men in the latter verse has the same meaning as men in *Choose us out men* (Ex. 17:9) and in *all of them men* (Num. 13:3).²²⁵ in Deut. 1:13 means the same as *anshe chayil* in Ex. 18:21 even though the wording is different. Jethro said appoint men.

²²⁰ See I.E. on Ex. 11:5 and Gen. 5:29.

I.E. makes this point here because, as he goes on to note, there are discrepancies between our chapter and the first chapter of Deuteronomy with regard to the description of the quality of the judges chosen by Moses.
²²² The appointment of judges.
²²³ Hebrew, anshe chayil.
²²⁴ Rather than get you able men,
²²⁵ The meaning of men in both of these verses is, men of valor, for both verses deal with tasks requiring such men. Thus anashim

ואמר יראי אלהים, שאין להם יראה מאדם רק מהשם לבדו, וכנגדם אמר משה, חכמים ונבונים (דבר' א יג) כי לא יתכן להיות ירא שמים כראוי רק מי שהוא חכם:


SUCH AS FEAR GOD. Who do not fear men but fear only God. It was to them that Moses was referring when he said,²²⁶ *wise…and understanding* (Deut. 1:13).²²⁷ For it is not possible for one to be a fearer of heaven unless one be wise.

ואמר יתרו אנשי אמת, שאינם כזבנים: **שונאי בצע.** ממון והם נודעים ככה למראה עיני אדם, וכנגדם אמר משה, וידועים (דבר' א יג):


Jethro continued: MEN OF TRUTH. Who do not lie. HATING UNJUST GAIN (*betza*). Money.²²⁸ (unjust gain) means money. So too Rashi. People who appear so, and are known as such by the community. It was in reference to these that Moses said, *and known* (Deut. 1:13).²²⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:21:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:21:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:21:4)


**שרי אלפים.** יש לתמוה, אם פי' אלה השרים כמשמעם, יהיה מספרם יותר משבעים אלף וט' אלפים וזה רחוק מאוד להיות שרים רבים כאלה, והכתוב אמר, בפשע ארץ רבים שריה (משלי כח ב), ועוד איך יתכן להיות שמינית המחנה ראשי שבטים, כי כן אמר משה, ואקח את ראשי שבטיכם (דבר' א טו) ותמצא בהם כל המדות הטובות הנזכרות, והם מיוצאי מצרים שלמדו מעשיהם, וכתוב כמעשה ארץ מצרים (ויקרא יח ג), והנה דור המדבר שלמדם משה מ' שנה, ולא הוצרכו לעשות אומנות כי לחמם נתן, ומימיהם נאמנים, והמן מפקח, הפך המינים שהתאוו מה שאין רגילים לאכול במצרים, ומשה אמר להם בשנת הארבעים, ולא נתן ה' לכם לב לדעת (דבר' כט ג) והנה יש לתמוה, איך ימצא המספר הנזכר שיהיו כולם חכמים ונבונים, והנכון בעיני, כי שרי אלפים הם שתחת ידם אלף איש עבדיו או נעריו או שכיריו אולי אלה הם ראשי השבטים, והיה מספרם שנים עשר, ושרי המאות הם רבים, ושרי חמשים, כדרך וחמשים איש רצים לפניו (ש"ב טו א):


RULERS OF THOUSANDS. One may wonder: If the meaning of the term rulers is here to be taken literally, then their number comes to more that seventy-nine thousand.²³⁰ (Ex. 38:26). The number of rulers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens of such a group comes to 79,650 (Krinsky). Now, it is extremely far-fetched for there to have been so many rulers. Indeed, Scripture states, *For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof* (Prov. 28:2).²³¹ Furthermore, how is it possible for an eighth of the camp to be heads of the tribes? For this is what Moses said, that is, *So I took the heads of your tribes*²³² (Deut. 1:15). Additionally, how is it possible that all of the above-mentioned virtues²³³ were found in these people who came out of Egypt and learned their ways? Indeed, Scripture states, *After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do* (Lev. 18:3).²³⁴ Now the desert generation, who were taught by Moses for forty years, did not have to work, for their bread was freely given and their water faithfully delivered. The manna, which they were not in the habit of eating in Egypt, in contrast to the types of food which they desired,²³⁵ instilled wisdom. Nevertheless, Moses told this generation at the end of forty years, *but the Lord hath not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day* (Deut. 29:3). We are thus amazed as to how it was possible to find the above-noted number²³⁶ of wise and understanding men.²³⁷ It appears to me that *the rulers of thousands* were men who had under them a thousand people, namely, slaves, young men, or hired hands. It is possible that these were the heads of the tribes and that they numbered twelve. The rulers of hundreds were many. The rulers of fifties were so called after the manner of *and fifty men to run before him* (II Sam. 15:1).²³⁸

footnotes:
²³⁰ The Israelites numbered six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men
²³¹ Translated according to I.E. A surfeit of rulers is a punishment for a people. Why then would Moses appoint so many rulers over Israel?
²³² The verse continues: And made them heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens.
²³³ Able men, God-fearing men, truthful men, etc.
²³⁴ Which implies that Israelites followed Egyptian practice. Otherwise why tell them not to do so?
²³⁵ See Num. 11:5.
²³⁶ Over 79,000.
²³⁷ So soon after the Exodus when, as noted in Deut. 29:3, forty years later such men were a rarity.
²³⁸ That is, they each had fifty servants. Thus ruler over thousands, hundreds, etc., does not refer to judges in charge of a thousand Israelites, a hundred Israelites, etc., but to the amount of wealth possessed by the people from whom the judges were chosen.

### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:23:1)


**וי"ו ויכלת.** כפ"א רפה בלשון ישמעאל אם תעשה את הדבר הזה, ויתן לך השם רשות לעשותו אז תוכל לעמוד והנה מלת עמוד שם הפועל, כמו עמוד פתח האהל (שופ' ד כ) גם פשטה וערה וחגורה על חלצים (ישעי' לב יא):


THEN THOU SHALT BE ABLE. The *vav* of *ve-yakholta* (then thou shalt be able)²³⁹ can be taken to mean: and thou shalt be able. Hence I.E.’s comment that it means: then thou shalt be able. is like the Arabic *fah*.²⁴⁰ If you do this thing, and God grants you permission to do it, then you will be able to endure. Now the word *amod* (endure) is an infinitive. It is like the word *amod* (stand)²⁴¹ in *Stand in the door of the tent* (Jud. 4:20). *Peshotah* (strip you) *ve-orah* (and make you bare), *va-chagorah* (and gird) in *Strip you, and make you bare, and gird sackcloth upon your lions* (Is. 32:11) are also infinitives.

²³⁹ Va-yakholta
²⁴⁰ It does not necessarily mean “and.” See I.E. on Gen. 1:2 and the notes thereto.
²⁴¹ Which is an infinitive.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:23:2)


וטעם וגם כל העם הזה, כי בעלי הריב שהיו נצבים לפניו, יש מהם שלא יוכל לדבר אליך לשפטם והנה בשובם לאהליהם תתחזק המריבה ביניהם, רק עתה יבא כל אחד על מקומו שהוא אהלו בשלום:


[AND ALL THIS PEOPLE ALSO SHALL GO TO THEIR PLACE IN PEACE.] Its meaning is, when some the disputants who were standing before Moses were not able to present their cases before him²⁴² for adjudication, their conflict intensified when they returned to their tents. However, now²⁴³ each one would return to his place, that is, his tent, in peace.

### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:24:1)


**וטעם וישמע.** הזכיר עצת יתרו ולא הזכיר עצתו שהוא הוסיף על עצת יתרו, והוא ששם שוטרים על השבטים לעשות מה שיצוו השופטים, וכן כתוב ושוטרים לשבטיכם (דבר' א טו) וכתוב, שופטים ושוטרים תתן לך בכל שעריך (שם טז יח):


[SO MOSES HEARKENED.] Scripture mentions Jethro’s council but does not mention Moses’ council.²⁴⁴ Moses added to Jethro’s council: that is, Moses placed officers over the tribes to enforce the decrees of the judges. Scripture thus reads, *and officers, tribe by tribe* (Deut. 1:15), and *Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates* (Deut. 16:18).

footnotes:
²⁴⁴ Scripture in our chapter notes that Jethro advised Moses to appoint judges and that Moses followed his advice. However, it omits telling us that Moses decided not only to appoint judges but to appoint officers as well.



### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:25:1)


**ויבחר משה אנשי חיל.** שהיה דבר ברור ולא הזכיר יראי אלהים כי הוא לבדו ידע לבב אנוש ומשה אמר כי בחר לנו אנשים חכמים כי יוכל לדעת זה רק יש חכם שאיננו ירא שמים והזכיר ידועים שהם למראה העין, ולא הזכירם עתה כי אחז דרך קצרה:


AND MOSES CHOSE ABLE MEN. This thing was ascertainable. *Such as fear God*²⁴⁵ is not mentioned, for only God knows what is in a person’s heart. Moses said that he chose wise men for us, for he was able to ascertain this. However, there are wise men who are not God-fearing. Moses mentioned²⁴⁶ men *who are known* (Deut. 1:13),²⁴⁷ that is, men whom people recognize. He did not mention them here because he was being brief.

### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 18:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/18:26:1)


**ישפוטו הם.** כמו ישפוטו בשורק תחת חולם כמו וגם לא תַעבוּרי מזה (רות ב ח) כמו ולא תעבוֹרי, ור' שלמה רצה להפריש ביניהם ולא עלתה בידו ונוכל לומר דרך דקדוק, כי ראינו חָדְלוּ פרזון בישראל חָדֵלּוּ (שופטים ה ז) בדגשות הלמ"ד בעבור שהוא באתנח, הרים נָזֹלּוּ (ישעי' סג יט) בסוף פסוק, ואמר תְהָתֵלּוּ בו (איוב יג ט) כי חשבוהו כמו סוף פסוק, כי מלת "בו" דבקה היא עם "תהתלו" ותנועה אחת לבדה וככה יִשְׁפְטוּ הם, כמו יִשְׁפוּטוּ בעבור שיש להשיב כי אין כח האתנח ככח סוף פסוק "בו", הנה עמים תחתיך יִפְלוּ (תה' מה ו) ה' על יְמִינְךָ (שם קי ה) טוב עשית עם עַבְדְךָ (שם קיט סה) ורבים כאלה, וככה לא ימצא בסוף פסוק:


THEY JUDGED THEMSELVES. *Yishputu* (judged) means the same as *yishpotu* (judged).²⁴⁸ A *shuruk* has been substituted for a *cholam* in *yishputu.* It is similar to *lo ta’avuri* (neither pass) in *neither pass from hence* (Ruth 2:5), which has the same meaning as *ve-lo ta’avori* (and neither pass).²⁴⁹ the more common form. However, Rabbi Solomon²⁵⁰ wanted to distinguish between them²⁵¹ and *yishpotu.* Rashi implies that *yishpotu* is an imperative and *yishputu* a participle. See Rashi on verse 26. but was unable to do so.²⁵² Now from a grammatical standpoint the following may be said. We find the terms *chadelu* (ceased)²⁵³ and *chadellu* (ceased) with a *dagesh* in the *lamed* because it is marked with an *etnach*²⁵⁴ in *The rulers ceased* (chadelu) *in Israel, they ceased* (chadellu) (Jud. 5:7). We similarly find the word *nazollu*²⁵⁵ the usual form. (quake) at the end of a verse in *That the mountains may quake* (Is. 63:19). Scripture likewise reads, *tehatellu*²⁵⁶ the usual form. *vo* (will ye mock him) (Job 13:9) since *tehatellu* is considered²⁵⁷ to be the last word, etc. to be the last word in the sentence because it is connected to the word *vo,* which has only one vowel. Similarly, *yishpetu hem* is like *yishputu* (hem),²⁵⁸) comes in the middle of a sentence and the other (*yishputu*) at the end of a sentence. for one can say²⁵⁹ and the *sof pasuk* equally change the word’s vocalization. Hence *yishpetu* and *yishputu* should be vocalized in the same way. that the *etnach*²⁶⁰ does not have the same power that the end of the verse has. Observe the word *yippelu* (fall) in *The peoples fall under thee* (Ps. 45:6); *yeminekha* (thy right hand) in *The Lord at thy right hand* (Ps. 110:5); *avdekha* (thy servant) in *Thou hast dealt well with Thy servant* (Ps. 119:65)²⁶¹ beneath them and maintain their normal vowels. Similarly *yishpetu.* and many other such instances. We do not find this to be the case at the close of a verse.²⁶²

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:1:1)


**בחדש השלישי.** לא ידענו טעם ביום הזה אם לא יהיה פי' ר' משה נכון, שהוא ראש חדש כמו מחר חדש (ש"א כ יח) והזכיר הכתוב זה כי אחר ימים מועטים ליום חנותם היה מתן תורה אולי יום אחד עלה אל השם וירד ודבר עם ישראל וביום השלישי לחדש עלה פעם אחרת להשיב אל השם דברי העם, ושם נאמר לו כי ביום השלישי יהיה מתן תורה, וכל זה מדרך הסברא, כי על הקבלה נסמוך שבששה בסיון נתנה התורה ועל דרך העבור, יום ששי בשבוע היה אם לא היה חדש אייר מעובר אולי טעם ביום הזה כי רחוק מרפידים ובין הר סיני היה רב יותר ממרחק כל מסע:


IN THE THIRD MONTH. We do not know the meaning of *the same day* (ba-yom ha-zeh)¹ unless the interpretation of Rabbi Moses² to the effect that it³ (in the month) which opens our verse. See note 5. refers to the new moon is correct.⁴ 86b), the *Mekhilta* (*Parshat Yitro*), and Rashi, as well. Ibn Ezra apparently quoted Rabbi Moses’ opinion because it can be linguistically defended, while the Talmud derives it from a *gezerah shavah.* See *Sabbath* 86b. Also see next note. It is like *Tomorrow is the new moon* (I Sam 20:18).⁵ (in the third month). According to Rabbi Moses the word *chodesh* means new moon, as in I Sam. 20:18 which reads *machar ha-chodesh* (tomorrow is the new moon). According to Rabbi Moses our verse should be interpreted as follows: On the third new moon, i.e., on the first day of the third month after the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day, i.e., on the aforementioned new moon, came they into the wilderness of Sinai. It should be noted that on Ex. 12:2, I.E. quotes Rabbi Moses as saying that the term *rosh chodesh* (new moon) is tautological because the word *chodesh* by itself means new moon. Scripture notes this⁶ because the Torah was given a few days after Israel camped.⁷ Perhaps Moses went up to God⁸ on day one⁹ and then came down and spoke to Israel.¹⁰ Then on the third day of the month he went up again to report the words of the people to God.¹¹ It was then told to Moses that the giving of the Torah would take place on the third day.¹² All of this is by way of logical exegesis because we accept the tradition¹³ 86b. that the Torah was given on the sixth day of Sivan.¹⁴ 86b: “The Decalogue was given on the sixth (of the month of Sivan). Rabbi Jose says on the seventh.” According to the rules of the calendar, if¹⁵ a day was not added to the month of Iyyar,¹⁶ then the Torah was given on a Friday.¹⁷ 87b), Israel left Egypt on a Thursday. Now if the new moon at that time was not consecrated by observation but rather by following the rules of the Hebrew calendar, then the sixth of Sivan had to fall on a Friday. See chapter 1 of the *Mekhilta* on the Torah portion *Be-Shallach.* It is possible that Scripture reads, *the same day* because the distance¹⁸ as in *Vat. Ebr.* 38 rather than *rachok* as in the printed editions. from Rephidim and Mount Sinai was greater than the distance between each journey.¹⁹ refers to the day that they left Rephidim. Our verse thus tells us that Israel came to the wilderness of Sinai on the same day that they left Rephidim. Scripture notes this because unlike the other journeys, which were normally a day’s journey apart, Rephidim and Sinai were far apart. Yet Israel made the journey in one day. From this comment it is clear that I.E. had serious doubts about whether *ba-chodesh ha-shelishi* really means on the first day of the third month.

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:9:1

**ויאמר.** אחר שאמר וישב משה, מה טעם לומר ויגד משה את דברי העם אל ה', דע כי פסוקים רבים בתורה שהיו ראוים להיותם מוקדמים, והנה פירושם וכבר היה כך וכך, כמו ויצר ה' אלהים (ברא' ב ז) וכבר יצר, ויצמח ה' אלהים (שם שם ט) וכבר הצמיח, ויאמר בת מי את (שם כד כג) וכבר אמר, וכן כתוב "ואשאל אותה ואומר" ואחר כך ואשים הנזם על אפה (שם שם מז) ותאמר אל העבד (שם שם סה) וכבר אמרה אל העבד, אז ותפול מעל הגמל (שם שם סד) ואין צורך להאריך, והנה זה ויגד משה, וכבר הגיד ולא הזכיר הכתוב מה הגיד, ומלת הגיד לעולם על דבר חדש שלא הזכירו והנה איננו דבק עם וישב משה ומתשובת השם שאמר הנה אנכי בא אליך בעב הענן למדנו מה הגיד, ועוד מצאנו זה הדבר מפורש בדברי משה כאשר אפרש, דע כי מצרים והודו הם מבני חם, ואלה סומכין על אלה, ואנשי הודו אינם אוכלים בשר, וכך היו עושים המצרים, ולא נשתנו מזה המנהג רק בעבור שהתגבר עליהם מלכות ישמעאל ושבו לדתו, וחכמי הודו נותנין ראיות כפי מחשבתם, כי לא יתכן שידבר השם עם אדם וחי וישראל היו במצרים והיו בהם אנשים על דעת האמונה הזאת והיתה נבואת משה בספק אצלם ואין טענה ממלת ויאמינו בה' ובמשה עבדו (למעלה יד לא) כי כתוב וירא ישראל ולא כל ישראל, ואילו היה כתוב כל ישראל, ידבר על הרוב כמשפט הלשון, כמו וימת כל מקנה מצרים (למעלה ט, ו) ואחר כן כתוב, שלח העז את מקנך (שם שם יט):


AND THE LORD SAID. What reason is there for saying, *And Moses told the words of the people unto the Lord* (v. 9) after having said,⁶⁶ *And Moses reported the words of the people unto the Lord*? Note that there are many verses in the Torah that should have come earlier.⁶⁷ Their meaning is that such and such already took place.⁶⁸ For example, the meaning of *va-yitzar* (formed) in, *Then the Lord God formed*⁶⁹ (Gen. 2:7) is, He⁷⁰ had already formed;⁷¹ the meaning of *va-yatzmach* (made to grow) in *And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow* (Gen. 2:9) is, He had already made to grow;⁷² the meaning of *va-yomer* (and said) in *and said: Whose daughter art thou?* (Gen. 24:23) is, and he⁷³ had already said.⁷⁴ before giving Rebekah a ring and bracelets. See I.E. on Gen. 24:14 and the notes thereto. Indeed, Scripture explicitly states,⁷⁵ *And I asked her, and said* (Gen. 24:47),⁷⁶ and then,⁷⁷ *I put the ring upon her nose* (*Ibid.*). Similarly, the meaning of *And she*⁷⁸ *said unto the servant* (Gen. 24:65) is, and she had already said unto the servant,⁷⁹ and then, *she alighted from the camel* (Gen. 24:64).⁸⁰ There is no need to elaborate.⁸¹ Now the meaning of *And Moses told* here⁸² is, and Moses had already told. Scripture does not mention what Moses told.⁸³ The word *higid* (told) always refers to something new that has not previously been mentioned. It is thus not connected to *and Moses reported*.⁸⁴ (verse 9) does not refer to *and Moses reported.* From God’s answer to Moses, “*Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud*” (v. 9), we learn what Moses told.⁸⁵ Furthermore, as I will explain,⁸⁶ we find this clearly stated in Moses’ very words. Note that the Egyptians and the Indians are from the children of Ham. Each one relies on the other.⁸⁷ The people of India do not eat meat. The Egyptians used to do the same. They changed their practice only because the kingdom of Ishmael⁸⁸ overpowered them and they accepted the religion of the Ishmaelites. The Indian sages offer proofs in accordance with their thinking that it is impossible for God to talk to a person and for that person to live. Now the Israelites were in Egypt.⁸⁹ There were among them people who followed this belief.⁹⁰ They were in doubt about Moses’ prophecy. *And they believed in the Lord, and in His servant Moses* (Ex. 14:31) does not dispute this.⁹¹ For Scripture reads, *And Israel saw* (*Ibid.*). It does not say: and all Israel saw.⁹² opens with *And Israel saw.* Since the latter only applies to a part of the people, so does the former. Hence *And they believed in the Lord, and his servant Moses* refers to part of the people, not to all of the people. Even if it read, all of Israel,⁹³ it would speak of the majority as is the style of the language,⁹⁴ as in *and all the cattle of Egypt died* (Ex. 9:6),⁹⁵ (Ex. 9:4). which is followed by *Now therefore send, hasten in thy cattle* (Ex. 9:19).⁹⁶ means: and most of the cattle of Egypt died.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:1)


**לא תגע בו.** מלת "בו" שבה אל האדם הנוגע בהר והטעם לא יכנס אדם אחריו לתפשו רק יסקלוהו הרואים ממקום מעמדם מיד, ואם רחוק יורוהו בחצים:

The word *bo* (him) refers to the person who touches the mount.¹¹² also means “it.” Thus our verse may be taken to mean, no hand shall touch it, that is, the mountain (see previous note). Hence I.E.’s comment. It means that no one shall enter after him¹¹³ to grab him. ###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:2)


**ומלת יירה.** משונה מרעותה כי משפט בעלי היו"ד להתחלף בוי"ו בעתיד בנין נפעל כמו ולא יִוָדַע השבע (ברא' מא לא) יסרתני וָאִוָסֵר (ירמי' לא יז) אולי עשו כך שלא תתערב עם גזרת למען **תורא** (תה' קל, ג) כי האלף והה"א נחים בסוף המלה, אין הפרש ביניהם במבטא:


[SHOT THROUGH.] The word *yiyareh* (shot through) differs from its counterparts.¹¹⁴ as their first letter. The root of *yiyareh* is *yod, resh, heh.* For the rule pertaining to roots that have a *yod* as their first letter is that the *yod* changes to a *vav* in the *nifal* imperfect, as in the word *yivvada* (be known)¹¹⁵, *dalet, ayin.* in *and the plenty shall not be known* (Gen. 41:31) and *va-ivvaser* (and I was chastised)¹¹⁶ in *Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised* (Jer. 31:18). Perhaps they¹¹⁷ did this so that this root¹¹⁸ not be confused with the root of *tivvare* (thou mayest be feared)¹¹⁹, *resh, alef.* in *That Thou mayest be feared* (Ps. 130:4).¹²⁰ (cast) and *yara* (feared) were conjugated in the exact same way in the *nifal* imperfect, it would be hard to distinguish one from the other. Hence in one the *yod* changed into a *vav,* as is the rule, and in the other the *yod* remained unchanged. For the *alef* and the *heh* are silent at the end of the word and there is no difference in pronunciation between them.¹²¹

¹¹⁸ Yod, resh, heh.
¹¹⁹ From the root yod
¹²⁰ In other words, if yarah
¹²¹ Hence it is easy to confuse these two words.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:13:4)


**במשוך היובל.** פי' כבש, ונקרא היובל כן, בעבור והעברת שופר תרועה (ויקרא כה, ט) כי שופר הוא מקרני הכבש, וכן כתוב במשוך בקרן היובל בשמעכם את קול השופר (יהושע ו ה) והתימה על האומרים, כי על קול השופר הולך וחזק מאד, משה ידבר במשוך היובל, כי קול השופר הוא פלא גדול, אין במעמד הר סיני גדול ממנו כי קולות וברקים וענן כבד גם הם נראים בעולם, וקול שופר לא נשמע עד יום עשרת הדברים והנה לא היה מקרן כבש:


WHEN THE RAM’S HORN SOUNDETH LONG. *Yovel* (ram) is a lamb.¹²² which is made from a ram’s horn, is by extension referred to as a *yovel.* Thus *bi-meshokh ha-yovel* is to be rendered: when the ram’s horn soundeth long. I.E. uses the term *keves,* which means a lamb. He probably meant a ram. See *Rosh Ha-Shanah* 26a. Jubilee (*yovel*) is so called because Scripture states, *Then shalt thou make proclamation with the blast of a shofar*¹²³ (Lev. 25:9), and the *shofar* is made from the horns of a lamb.¹²⁴ is so called because it is inaugurated by the sounding of the *shofar,* which is made from a ram’s horn. It is similarly written, *And it shall be, that when they make a long blast with the horn of the yovel,*¹²⁵ *and when ye hear the sound of the shofar*¹²⁶ and *yovel* refer to one and the same thing. (Josh. 6:5). One must wonder at those who say that *And when the voice of the horn waxed louder and louder, Moses spoke* (v. 19) refers to *when the ram’s horn*¹²⁷ *soundeth long*.¹²⁸ For the voice of the horn¹²⁹ was a great wonder;¹³⁰ there was no greater wonder at that assembly around Mount Sinai. For sounds of thunder, lightning, and a thick cloud are also visible in the world. However, the voice of the horn¹³¹ was unheard of until the day of the Decalogue.¹³² Behold, the sound¹³³ spoken of in verse 19. was not from the horn of a lamb.¹³⁴

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:13:6

**המה יעלו בהר.** אמר ר' שמואל בן חפני, כי טעם המה, אהרן ובניו ושבעים זקנים, שכתוב עליהם "ואל משה אמר עלה את ה' אתה ואהרן נדב ואביהוא ושבעים מזקני ישראל" (כד א) ולשאר ישראל לא נתן רשות לעלות אל הר סיני, על כן אמר המה ולא אחרים ודבריו טובים בעיני כי הכבוד היה תמיד על ההר עד שנעשה המשכן דכתיב, וכבוד ה' מלא את המשכן (מ לד) אז דבר עם משה באהל מועד אולי אז תקע משה בשופר, ונתן לו רשות לעלות בהסתלק הכבוד:


THEY SHALL COME UP TO THE MOUNT. Rabbi Samuel ben Hofni says that “they” refers to Aaron, Aaron’s sons, and the seventy elders concerning whom it is written, *And unto Moses He said: Come up unto the Lord, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel* (Ex. 24:1).¹³⁹ means when the ram’s horn soundeth long after the revelation. Rabbi Samuel thus disagrees with Saadiah’s interpretation that the reference is to the Day of Atonement when Moses descended Sinai. However, Moses did not give permission to the rest of the people to ascend Mount Sinai. He therefore said “they” and not others. His words appear good in my sight. For the glory was continually on Sinai until the tabernacle was erected, as it is written, *and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle* (Ex. 4:34). God then spoke with Moses in the tent of meeting. Perhaps Moses then sounded the horn¹⁴⁰ and now that the glory was gone,¹⁴¹ God gave him¹⁴² permission to ascend.¹⁴³

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/19:15:1)


**היו נכונים לשלשת ימים.** טעמו ליום השלישי ולפי הפשט לא הוסיף יום אחד מדעתו והנה אתן לך שני עדים נאמנים ושניהם בספר הזה הנה כתוב, ויאסוף אותם אל משמר שלשת ימים (ברא' מב יז), ושם כתוב ויאמר אליהם יוסף ביום השלישי (שם שם יח) וכתיב ובעוד שלשת ימים ישא פרעה (שם מ יט) ושם כתוב ויהי ביום השלישי יום הלדת (שם שם כ), וכן היו נכונים לשלשת ימים:


BE READY AGAINST THE THIRD DAY. The meaning of *li-sheloshet yamim* is, for the third day. According to the plain meaning of the text, Moses did not add a day by himself.¹⁴⁵ (and be ready against the third day). However, our verse reports that Moses told Israel, *heyu nekhonim li-sheloshet yamim* (be ready against the third day). According to the Rabbinic sage Rabbi Jose, Moses told Israel be ready for three days (which is the literal meaning of *heyu nekhonim li-sheloshet yamim*). That is, God will reveal himself to you on the fourth day. Moses thus added another day on his own. See *Sabbath* 87a. I will bring two faithful witnesses,¹⁴⁶ and *la-yom ha-shelishi.* both of which are found in this book. Now it is written, *And he put them all together into ward three days* (sheloset yamim) (Gen. 42:17). It is then written, *And Joseph said unto them the third day* (yom ha-shelishi) (Gen. 42:18). Scripture also states, *within yet three days* (sheloshet yamim) *shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee* (Gen. 40:19). It is then written, *And it came to pass the third day* (ba-yom ha-shelishi) (Gen. 40:20).¹⁴⁷ and *yom ha-shelishi.* Hence they must have one meaning. Similarly here, *heyu nekhnim li-sheloshet yamim* [means be ready for the third day].
